Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 1:

Tafsir Surat al-Nisa' (Commentary on the Chapter of Women)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

He said: Know that this surah is called Surat al-Nisa' (the Chapter of Women), and it is also called Surat al-Ahkam (the Chapter of Legal Rulings). It is Madani according to the view of most exegetes, except for the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾, for this verse was revealed in Makkah concerning the keys of the Ka'bah. Al-Nahhas reported that the surah is Makki.

It is related in a hadith: "Whoever recites Surat al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, and al-Nisa' in one night, will be recorded among the devoutly obedient (al-qanitin)." And it is related from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Learn Surat al-Baqarah, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, Surat al-Nur, and al-Ahzab, for in them are the obligatory duties (al-fara'id)."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O mankind﴾. Alqamah said: Everything in the Qur'an that begins with ﴿O mankind﴾ was revealed in Makkah, and everything in the Qur'an that begins with ﴿O you who have believed﴾ was revealed in Madinah.

And His saying: ﴿O you﴾ — "ya" is for calling, "ay" is for indicating, and "ha" is for alerting — ﴿fear your Lord﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "Fear Allah (Allah) your Lord."

He began the surah with exhortation and warning, saying: ﴿Fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul﴾. By "the single soul" he meant Adam, peace be upon him. He said ﴿single﴾ in the feminine only because of the wording, since nafs (soul) is feminine. This is like the words of the poet:

(Your father is a caliph whom another woman bore, and you are a caliph of that perfection)

He said "bore" (waladathu) only in view of the word khalifah, even though its meaning is masculine. ﴿And created of it its mate﴾, meaning Hawwa' (Eve). Hawwa' was so named because she was created from a living being (hayy). In the narratives it is related that Allah the Exalted created Hawwa' from a rib of Adam on his left side, which is called "al-qasira'". And in the well-known report: "Woman was created from a crooked rib; if you try to straighten her, you will break her, and if you leave her, you will enjoy her with her crookedness." It was also said that Hawwa' was created from dust.

His saying: ﴿and created of it its mate﴾ means: and created from its kind its mate, that is, from dust. The more correct view is the first. In the report: when Allah the Exalted created Adam, He cast sleep upon him, then took a rib from his ribs and created Hawwa' from it, and she sat beside him. When he awoke, he saw her sitting beside him. It was also said: taking the rib did not harm him in any way, for had it harmed him, a man would never have shown tenderness toward a woman.

And from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah the Exalted created the man from dust, and his understanding is in the dust; and He created the woman from the man, and her understanding is in the man; so keep your women confined.

﴿And He spread from both of them many men and women﴾. All of this is mentioned to demonstrate power and to manifest favour. ﴿And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another﴾, that is, you ask through Him, as when a man says: "I ask you by Allah" and "I adjure you by Allah." It was also said: its meaning is: fear Allah, by whom you make covenants, as when you say: "upon you is the covenant of Allah" and "upon me is the covenant of Allah," and the like.

As for His saying: ﴿and the wombs (al-arham)﴾, Hamzah recited "al-arhami" with a kasra on the mim, and its construction would be: you ask through Him and through the wombs. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: the Arabs say: "I adjure you by Allah and by the womb." They considered this reading weak, and the well-known reading has a fatha on the mim, and its construction is: and fear the wombs, lest you sever them.

In the report: Allah the Exalted says: "I am the Most Gracious, and I created the womb and derived for it a name from My name; whoever joins it, I will join him, and whoever severs it, I will sever him."

And it is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah the Exalted prolongs the lives of disbelievers and increases their wealth, and has not looked upon them since He created them, out of hatred for them." It was asked: "Why is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Because of the maintaining of ties of kinship."

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Watchful over you﴾, that is, Guardian (hafiz).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 2:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And give the orphans their property﴾. He meant by this: handing over the wealth to them after they reach puberty. He called them "orphans" after puberty because of the recency of their state of orphanhood. The Quraysh used to call the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "the orphan of Abu Talib" for this reason.

﴿And do not substitute the bad [khabith] for the good [tayyib]﴾. In an irregular (shadhdh) recitation: "and do not exchange the bad for the good." Al-khabith is the unlawful (haram), and al-tayyib is the lawful (halal). The meaning of the statement is: do not consume the wealth of the orphans unlawfully and leave your own lawful wealth. Mujahid said: its meaning is: do not hasten to consume the unlawful, for the lawful will come to you.

﴿And do not consume their property along with your property [ila amwalikum]﴾. Al-Farra' said: its meaning is "along with" (ma'a) your property. Others said: "ila" does not carry the meaning of "ma'a"; rather it retains its literal sense, and the meaning is: do not consume their property added to your property.

﴿Indeed, that is a great sin [huban kabiran]﴾. Al-hub is sin (ithm). In a report: "Abu Ayyub al-Ansari wanted to divorce his wife Umm Ayyub, so the Prophet (ﷺ) said: Indeed, the divorce of Umm Ayyub is a sin (lahawb)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly with the orphans﴾ means: that you will not be just. It is said: aqsata, when he was just, and qasata, when he acted unjustly. There are two opinions regarding the meaning of the verse. The first is that reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, namely what al-Zuhri narrated from Urwah that he asked Aisha about the matter of this verse, and she said: "O nephew, the verse was revealed concerning an orphan girl who is in the guardianship of her guardian, who desires her wealth and her beauty, and does not act justly regarding her dowry; so they were forbidden to marry them, and were commanded to marry others."

According to this, the meaning of the verse is: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly regarding marrying the orphans﴾; ﴿then marry what seems good to you of women, two, three, or four﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: the restriction of marriage to four women was for the sake of the orphans' wealth. If it is asked: how is this known, and how does this fit with that? It is answered: its meaning is that when God, exalted is He, was strict regarding the wealth of orphans, the Muslims became extremely scrupulous about it, and they began to marry women casually and made light of it; so the verse was revealed, and He intended: just as you were scrupulous regarding the wealth of orphans out of fear of injustice, be scrupulous also about exceeding four out of fear of injustice and partiality. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿then marry what seems good to you﴾, that is, what is lawful for you, ﴿of women, two, three, or four﴾, that is, do not exceed four.

Some people held that marrying nine is permissible by the apparent sense of this verse, because "two, three and four" makes nine; this is not correct. Rather, there are two opinions on it. The first: al-Zajjaj said: "two by two, three by three, four by four," meaning for each person. It was also said that the "waw" (and) carries the sense of "aw" (or), meaning: two, or three, or four. Moreover, according to the reading they mention, the expression would be defective, since whoever wished to mention nine would say "two, three and four," which is considered a flaw in speech. And He said: ﴿But if you fear that you will not act justly, then one﴾; because that is lighter in burden, ﴿or what your right hands possess﴾, because the rights over one's right-hand possessions are lesser than the rights of marriage. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿That is more suitable that you not deviate﴾, that is, that is nearer to your not being unjust. It is said: "ala" (ya'ulu) when he acted unjustly, and "a'ala" (yu'ilu) when he had many dependants. The poet said:

(We followed the Messenger, and cast aside
the Messenger's command, and deviated in the scales.)

That is, they acted unjustly. It is also reported that the people of Kufa rebuked Uthman concerning something, and he said: "I am not just, so I will not deviate," meaning: I am not a balance; so I will not act unjustly.

Al-Shafi'i said: its meaning is: that is more suitable that your dependants not be numerous. Al-Azhari related from al-Kisa'i that he related from the Arabs: "ala yaulu" when one's dependants increased, and this supports the view of al-Shafi'i.

And give the women their dower (ṣadaqat) graciously (naḥlah). Ṣadaqah and ṣadāq are one and the same. (Naḥlah) means: as an obligation (tadayyunan). Ibn ʿAbbas said: its meaning is: an obligatory duty (farīḍah). The address is to the husbands, according to the more correct view. It has also been said that the address is to the guardians (awliyāʾ), because the people of the Jahiliyyah did not give the woman her dower; rather, the guardians would take it. So the address to the guardians is to give the woman her dower as a naḥlah, meaning: it is a gift to her from God.

﴿And if they, of their own accord, remit to you a part of it﴾ meaning: if they give up some of the dower willingly. The "min" here is for partition (lil-takhyīr), not for partial quantity (lil-tabʿīḍ), so that it is permissible for the woman to give away the entire dower. ﴿Then consume it with pleasure and ease﴾. Hanīʾ (pleasant, wholesome) refers to what is eaten without any disturbance, and marīʾ refers to that whose outcome is praiseworthy, meaning that it does not cause indigestion. It is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "If one of you falls ill, let him borrow three dirhams from his wife out of her dower, buy honey with them, mix it with rainwater, and then drink it; for it is a blessed cure, and a wholesome and pleasant (hanīʾ marīʾ) remedy."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 5:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And do not give the foolish your wealth﴾. Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by "the foolish" here is children and women. Al-Sha'bi said: "A woman is more foolish than any fool."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the meaning of the verse is: do not make the woman the means of support for the household in terms of livelihood; rather, you should be the ones who maintain the women in livelihood. As for His words ﴿which Allah has made for you a means of support﴾, qiyam (support) and qiwam (maintenance) are one and the same; that is, your wealth, which Allah has made a means of sustenance for your livelihood. Al-Zajjaj said: its implied sense is: the wealth which sustains you, so that you stand by means of it. ﴿And provide for them from it and clothe them﴾. It was said: its meaning is: provide for them from it. And it was said: the particle (min, "from") is in its essential sense, and its meaning is: make their allotments of provision and clothing out of it.

﴿And speak to them a kind word﴾. It was said: its meaning is: teaching them the religion and the laws (sharia'i'). It was also said: he meant by it: a fair promise. That is, you say to them: "If you travel and profit, I will give you such-and-such; if you fight and take booty, I will give you such-and-such." This is the "kind word."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 6:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And test the orphans﴾ means: test the orphans. Then some of them said: "We only test them after they reach puberty, and they are called orphans because their orphanhood is recent." The correct view is that He meant testing before puberty. Then they differed. As for the jurists, they said: one gives him a small amount of property and sends him to the market so that he may bargain over the goods; then, when it comes to the contract, the guardian (wali) concludes it. Others said: the boy himself concludes the contract, and this is permissible in a small matter, for the sake of testing.

As for what the exegetes (mufassirun) said: one gives him property and places the household expenses in his charge, and tests him in them. ﴿Until, when they reach marriageable age﴾ means: the time of puberty (al-hulm). ﴿Then if you perceive﴾ means: you sense and find ﴿in them maturity (rushd)﴾. Mujahid said: intellect. Sufyan al-Thawri said: intellect and good management of property. The position of al-Shafi'i is that rushd is righteousness in religion and good management of property.

﴿Then deliver to them their property﴾ commands the guardians to hand over the property to them upon puberty and maturity. ﴿And do not consume it extravagantly﴾ means: do not eat it wastefully. ﴿And hastily, lest they grow up﴾ means: do not hasten to consume the orphans' property out of fear that they will grow up and take their property.

﴿And whoever is wealthy, let him abstain﴾ means: let him abstain with his own wealth from the orphan's property. ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat reasonably﴾. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: if the guardian is poor, he eats from the orphan's property to the extent of need. He also said: "I, regarding this property, am like the guardian of an orphan: if I become rich, I abstain, and if I am in need, I eat." A group of scholars adopted this view, that he may eat an amount that meets his need. Some of them said: a coarse garment and barley bread. Al-Sha'bi and a group said: he eats from the orphan's property by way of a loan. Mujahid said: he does not eat at all, neither as a loan nor otherwise. He said: the verse is abrogated by the saying of the Almighty: ﴿Do not consume your properties among yourselves in falsehood, except that it be trade by mutual consent﴾. This is the view of most scholars, and on it is the fatwa: that he does not eat at all. Whoever says he may eat, says he takes an amount equal to his wage for the work of supervision.

It has been narrated that a man came to Ibn Abbas and said: "I have an orphan who owns camels; what may I take from them?" He said: "Do you tend their watering trough, and daub their mangy ones with tar?" He said: "Yes." Ibn Abbas said: "Take from their milk what does not harm their offspring and is not excessive in milking."

There is a fourth view concerning His saying ﴿let him eat reasonably﴾: it means the poor man eats from his own sustenance reasonably, and does not take excessively from it until his wealth is exhausted, so that he needs the orphan's property.

﴿And when you deliver to them their property, then have witnesses over them﴾ recommends calling witnesses, so that they do not deny it.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾ means: as Witness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, and for women there is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave﴾. The occasion of the revelation of the verse was that Aws ibn Thabit al-Ansari died and left three daughters, a wife called Umm Kajjah, and two paternal cousins: Arfajah and Suwayd. The two cousins came and took all the property. The people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) did not give inheritance to women from the deceased, and they would say: "None inherits our wealth except one who thrusts with spears and strikes with swords." So the verse was revealed. This was the first verse revealed concerning the inheritance of women in property.

﴿Of what is little or much of it, a share ordained﴾. The prescribed shares have been explained in the verses of inheritance.

The Words of the Exalted: "And when the division takes place, if relatives, orphans and the needy are present, then provide them from it." That is, the division of the estate in inheritance, when present are those of the deceased's relatives who do not inherit from him, or orphans, or the needy, "then provide them from it": give them something. "And speak to them a kind word": that is, say to them, "May Allah bless you."

Then they differed. Some of them said: the verse is abrogated (mansukh), so it is permissible to give them and permissible not to give them. It was also said: it is recommended (nadb), and it is preferable to give them something. Among them were those who said: if they divide gold and silver and the like, he should give them something; and if they divide houses, real estate, slaves, garments and the like, he should say to them, "May Allah bless you."

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 9:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And let those fear [Allah] who, if they were to leave behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ The occasion of revelation (sabab nuzul) of the verse: the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a man among them was about to die, would come to him and say to him: "Look to your own soul, O man, and make a bequest of your wealth, for your heirs will not avail you anything against Allah." They would sometimes urge him to bequeath all of his wealth. So the verse was revealed: ﴿And let those fear [Allah] who, if they were to leave behind them...﴾ That is: if they were to leave behind them ﴿weak offspring﴾, that is, young children, ﴿would be anxious for them﴾, or for their children. So let them fear for the children of others as they fear for their own children, for the children of the deceased have more right to his wealth than outsiders. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice﴾, that is, just words.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 10:

The saying of Allah Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the properties of orphans unjustly⦄ The verse was revealed concerning Handhalah ibn al-Shamardal. He had been appointed guardian over an orphan and consumed all of his wealth. It is also said that the verse was initially revealed concerning the disbeliever: ﴿They only consume into their bellies fire⦄, because their consuming of that leads to the Fire, so Allah called them consumers of the Fire. This is like the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever drinks from vessels of gold and silver, he only swallows the fire of Hell into his belly."

In a hadith: "Flames of fire will come forth from their bodies on the Day of Resurrection." In another narration: "The angel will come to them, open their mouths, and force coals into them." ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. And if there are only daughters, two or more, for them is two-thirds of what he leaves; and if there is only one, for her is half. And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he leaves, if he has a child. But if he has no child⦄ And [the Prophet] said: "This is the consequence of your consuming the property of the orphan."

He also said: "Whoever makes an orphan weep, it is incumbent upon Allah to make his eyes weep on the Day of Resurrection."

﴿And they will enter a blazing Fire⦄ That is, they will enter Hell. It is also said: they will witness a blazing Fire. Sa'ir (blazing fire) means a flaring fire, and it is one of the names of Hell.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 11:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾. Its meaning: Allah prescribes for you concerning your children. This is like His words, the Exalted: ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. That is what He has enjoined upon you﴾, meaning: He has made it obligatory upon you. ﴿For the male, the like of the portion of two females﴾.

The occasion of revelation of the verse: "Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' was martyred on the day of Uhud and left behind two daughters, a wife, and a brother. The brother came and took all the wealth. The wife came complaining to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the verse was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the brother and said: Give the two daughters two-thirds, give the wife one-eighth, and take the remainder."

As for His words ﴿For the male, the like of the portion of two females﴾, it means: if one leaves a son and a daughter, the estate is divided into three shares: two shares for the son and one share for the daughter. ﴿But if they are women, more than two, then for them is two-thirds of what he left.﴾ Most of the Companions and the scholars hold that for two daughters, and for three, it is two-thirds.

Ibn 'Abbas said: for two daughters is one-half, and two-thirds is only for three or more, adhering to the apparent meaning of the verse. The first view is more correct.

The meaning of His words ﴿if they are women, more than two﴾ is: if they are women, two or more. This is like His words: ﴿Then strike above the necks﴾, meaning: strike the necks and what is above them. It was also said that "above" (fawq) is extraneous (ṣila), and its implied sense is: if they are women, two. The term for a plural applies to two, because the plural is a expression for the gathering of a thing, and two and three are equal in it. Moreover, we have agreed that two sisters inherit two-thirds, and they are the daughters of the deceased's father; so two daughters inheriting two-thirds is more fitting, and they are his daughters through the backbone.

﴿But if there is only one, then for her is half﴾, and on this there is consensus. ﴿And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he left, if he has a child﴾, meaning: for the deceased. ﴿But if he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third﴾, and there is no dispute about this.

﴿But if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth﴾. Most of the Companions and the scholars hold that two brothers and three brothers reduce the mother's share from a third to a sixth.

Ibn 'Abbas said: three reduce, but two do not reduce, because it is stated with the plural form, and the least plural is three.

We have already explained that the term for a plural applies to two and to three.

Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "fa-li-ummihi al-sudus" with a kasra on the hamza, which is a dialectal form for "umm" (mother), while the well-known form has a damma.

"Min ba'di wasiyyatin yusa biha aw dayn" is read in two ways: "yūṣā" with a kasra on the ṣād, meaning the testator enjoins it, and "yūṣā" with a fatha on the ṣād, in the passive form, the agent not being named.

﴿Half of what your wives leave, if they have no child; but if they have a child, then for you is a quarter of what they leave, after any bequest they make or debt. And for them is a quarter of what you leave, if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you make or debt.﴾

It is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "You recite the bequest before the debt, while the debt is before the bequest," meaning in terms of settlement. Then they differed. Some said that "aw" (or) carries the meaning of "wa" (and), and the intent is to combine the two, and to show that inheritance is postponed after both together. Others said that "aw" retains its literal meaning, and its sense is: after a bequest, if there is a bequest, or a debt, if there is a debt; so inheritance is postponed after each of them. From this, its postponement after both when they are combined is known by way of priority.

His words ﴿Your fathers and your sons﴾, meaning: those who inherit from you, your fathers and your sons, ﴿you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾, meaning: you do not know which of them is more beneficial to you in religion and in this world.

Some of them think that fathers benefit, so sons would be more beneficial; and some think that sons are more beneficial, so fathers would be more beneficial; and you do not know, while I know who is most beneficial to you. I have arranged your affairs according to what contains wisdom and benefit, so take it and follow it. In the reports: "In Paradise a father will be in a high rank and his son in a lower rank, so the son asks Allah, the Exalted, and He raises him to his father's rank. And a son will be in a high rank and his father in a lower rank, so the father asks Allah, the Exalted, and He raises him to his son's rank." This is the meaning of the verse, ﴿you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾ in the Hereafter, and of higher rank, so that you may attain his rank.

﴿An obligation from Allah﴾, meaning: what has been decreed of the inheritance shares. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of the affairs of His servants, ﴿Wise﴾ in establishing the rulings.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And for you is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child. But if they have a child, for you is one-fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they make or debt.﴾ This concerns the inheritance of husbands, and there is consensus (ijma') on it. ﴿And for them is one-fourth of what you leave, if you have no child. But if you have a child, for them is one-eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you make or debt.﴾ This concerns the inheritance of wives, and there is no disagreement about it.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if a man leaves an inheritance as a kalala, or a woman,﴾ meaning: or a woman who leaves an inheritance as a kalala (kalala: one who dies without ascendants or descendants, and the term is discussed below). Some scholars said: the meaning of kalala is not known. It is narrated from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah departed from this world without explaining three things to us: the kalala, the caliphate, and usury (riba).

The correct view is that its meaning is known. Then they differed. Ibn ʿAbbas, in one narration, and it is one of the two narrations from ʿUmar, said: Indeed, kalala is the name for a deceased person who has no child, and the siblings inherit along with the father.

And al-Hakam ibn ʿUtayba said: Kalala is the name for a deceased person who has no child, and the siblings inherit along with the parent. These are two views among the anomalous (shadh) opinions of disagreement. The correct position has two views:

The first is the view of the people of Madina and Kufa, that kalala is the name for heirs among whom there is neither a child nor a parent. It is derived from the ikleel (crown), which is what surrounds both sides of the face. So kalala is the name for one who surrounds the two sides of the deceased: the brothers and sisters, the paternal uncles, and others like them, and there is no ascendant or descendant.

They cited as evidence the hadith of Jabir: "He was ill, and the Messenger of Allah came in to visit him, and he said: Indeed, only a kalala inherits from me." He had no child and no parent among his heirs, and he made kalala the name of the heir. This is supported by what was recited as a anomalous reading: "And if a man leaves an inheritance as a kalala" with the ra' pronounced with kasra and shadda.

The people of Basra said, and this is the view of Abu Bakr, ʿAli, Ibn Masʿud, and Zayd, and in the more authentic of the two narrations from Ibn ʿAbbas: kalala is the name for the deceased who has no child and no parent. This is the apparent meaning of the verse, and the other anomalous reading supports it: "And if a man leaves an inheritance as a kalala" with the ra' pronounced with fatha and shadda. A poet said:

(And the father of a man is his protector for him... and the client of the kalala does not get angry)

So he makes kalala a name for the deceased.

There is another view: that kalala is the name for the estate itself, said by ʿAta'. As for His saying: ﴿And he has a brother or a sister, then each of the two has one-sixth.﴾ They agreed that the intended brother and sister here are maternal siblings, and a fixed share of one-sixth is assigned to each of them, whether male or female.

﴿But if they are more than that, they are partners in the one-third.﴾ There is consensus that their fixed share is one-third when they are multiple, however many they are. ﴿After any bequest that is made or debt, without causing harm.﴾ That is, the testator must not harm the heirs by exceeding the one-third and the like. ﴿A commandment from Allah.﴾ That is, an obligation from Allah. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.﴾

Qur'an 4:13: "Those are the limits (ḥudūd) of Allah." That is: what has been mentioned of the prescribed, bounded obligations (furūḍ maḥdūda). "And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; and that is the great triumph." He mentions the reward of whoever obeys Him and does not transgress His limits.

﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits - He will admit him to a Fire, wherein he will abide eternally, and for him is a humiliating punishment.﴾

He mentions the punishment of the one who disobeys Him and transgresses His limits.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 15:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness﴾. Al-lātī (اللاتي), al-latī (اللاتي), and al-lawātī (اللواتي) are names for a group of women. The poet said:

(They are the ones called al-lawātī, al-latī, and al-lātī, who claim that I have grown old, my contemporaries.)

Similar to these is al-lā'ī (اللائي) as well. The poet said:

(Of those who did not perform the pilgrimage, you desire reward, but rather that they might kill the innocent, the heedless one.)

As for His words ﴿commit lewdness﴾, by lewdness (al-fāḥisha, الفاحشة) He means here adultery (al-zinā). ﴿Call four of your men to witness against them﴾: this is addressed to the rulers, meaning: seek four witnesses against them. This verse is the proof that adultery requires four witnesses. ﴿And if they testify, then confine them to the houses until death takes them or Allah makes for them a way.﴾ This was the ruling at the beginning of Islam: a woman who committed adultery was confined to the house until she died. Then this was abrogated (naskh, نسخ, abrogation) concerning the virgin (al-bikr, the unmarried woman) by flogging and exile (taghrīb), and concerning the previously married (al-thayyib) by flogging and stoning. This is the explanation of the "way" mentioned in the verse. The proof for this is the hadith of ʿUbāda: "Take from me, take from me; Allah has made for them a way: the virgin with the virgin, one hundred lashes and a year of exile; the previously married with the previously married, one hundred lashes and stoning with stones."

Then flogging was abrogated concerning the previously married, and their ruling settled on stoning.

Some scholars said: flogging together with stoning remains in effect as a ruling, but the first view is more correct.

Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions said: exile is also abrogated concerning the virgin, and the detail of this is mentioned in jurisprudence (fiqh).

They differed over whether that confinement in the house was by way of a prescribed punishment (ḥadd) or was imprisonment in order to make the punishment manifest. There are two views: one, that it was a ḥadd; and the second, that it was imprisonment in order to make the ḥadd manifest.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 16:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And those two of you who commit it, harm them﴾. The scholars differed concerning what is meant by the two verses. Mujahid said: the first verse concerns women, and this verse concerns men who commit fornication.

Others said: the first concerns the thayyib (previously married), and this verse concerns the virgins (abkar).

There is a third view: that the first verse concerns a woman who commits sihaq (lesbianism) with a woman, and the second verse concerns a man who has intercourse with a man. And it has been said: "If a man has intercourse with a man, then both are fornicators (zaniyan); and if a woman has intercourse with a woman, then both are fornicatresses (zaniyatan)."

The meaning of harm (idha') in this verse is: verbal abuse, making someone hear what is disliked, reproach, and striking with sandals.

If it is said: the first verse mentions confinement (habs), and the second mentions harm (idha'); how is the combination to be understood? It is said: according to the view of the one who said that the first verse concerns one category and the second verse concerns another category, the statement is consistent.

Some of them said: he intended by it the combination of harm and confinement in the case of the fornicator, so that he is first harmed and then confined. And the second verse, although it comes later in recitation, is earlier in meaning, as if he said: "And those two of you who commit the indecency, harm them and hold them in the house. ﴿But if they repent and make amends, then leave them alone﴾, i.e., turn away from harming them. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful.﴾"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Repentance with Allah is only for those who do evil in ignorance﴾. Qatadah said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) agreed that whoever disobeys Allah is ignorant (jahil). It was also said: He meant by it those who are ignorant of the true nature of Allah's punishment. And it was said: ignorance in disobedience is that one chooses fleeting pleasure over lasting pleasure.

﴿Then they repent soon﴾. He means: before death. Ad-Dahhak said: Everything between you and death is "soon." It was also said: He meant by it repentance before one witnesses the Angel of Death. And it was said: He meant by it: they repent before the death rattle (taghghur).

And in the report: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever repents a year before his death, Allah accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed, a year is (a long time)." Then he said: "Whoever repents a month before his death, Allah accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed, a month is a long time." Then he said: "Whoever repents a week before his death, Allah accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed, a week is (a long time)." Then he said: "Whoever repents a day before his death, Allah accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed, a day is a long time." (Whoever repents half a day before his death, Allah accepts his repentance; then he said: indeed, half a day is a long time.) "Whoever repents an hour before his death, Allah accepts his repentance." Then he said: "Indeed, an hour is a long time. Whoever repents before he is in the death rattle, Allah accepts his repentance." Narrated by Ubadah ibn al-Samit.

This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Then they repent soon; those are the ones to whom Allah turns back in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing, Wise﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 18:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And repentance is not for those who commit evil deeds﴾. It has been said: he meant by "evil deeds" shirk (associating partners with God). Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is hypocrisy (nifaq). It has also been said: all sins.

﴿Until when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now"﴾. He means the state of death: he repents when he is being driven (to death). The reason for this is like the repentance of Pharaoh when drowning overtook him; he said: "I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believed." God, exalted is He, says: there is no repentance for these people.

﴿Nor for those who die while they are disbelievers﴾. He means: nor for those who die as disbelievers there is repentance. ﴿Those — We have prepared for them﴾, i.e., We have readied for them ﴿a painful punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 19:

﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion.﴾ The verse was revealed concerning the Ansar. A man among them, when his father died, would inherit his father's wife. Then, if he wished, he would keep her for himself as a wife, and if he wished, he would marry her to someone else and take her dowry. And if he wished, he would prevent her from marrying (ʿadl) until she became distressed and ransomed herself with property. When Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat al-Ansari died, leaving his wife Kabisha bint Maʿn al-Ansari, his son Hisn came and inherited the woman. The woman came complaining to the Prophet (ﷺ), and then the saying of Allah, the Exalted, was revealed: ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion.﴾ It is also recited as "kurhan" with a ḍamma on the kaf. Al-kurh with a fatḥa means compulsion (al-ikrah), and al-kurh with a ḍamma means hardship (al-mashaqqa). ﴿And do not restrain them in order that you may take away part of what you have given them.﴾ That is, do not prevent them from marrying other men until they become distressed, so that they ransom themselves with part of their property. Thus this is addressed to the guardians of the deceased.

The correct view is that it is addressed to the husbands, meaning: if the wife is not willing, then do not keep her by harming her, so that she ransoms herself with part of her property. ﴿Unless they commit a clear immorality.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is nushuz (wifely disobedience). It was also said: it is adultery. That is, if she has committed nushuz or adultery, then it becomes lawful for him to take a ransom from her and take her property. At the beginning of Islam, when a woman committed adultery, the husband would take all of her dowry from her, and then this was abrogated (naskh). ﴿And live with them in kindness.﴾ That is, generosity in lodging, speech, and maintenance. ﴿But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes in it much good.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 20:

Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿And if you desire to replace one spouse with another spouse﴾. Here by "zawj" (spouse) he means "zawjah" (wife), and it is a term applying to both the man and the woman. ﴿And you have given one of them a heap of gold﴾ means: from the dowry. ﴿Then do not take from it anything. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾ means: by injustice (zulm), ﴿and a manifest sin﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 21:

﴿And how could you take it back when you have gone in unto one another?﴾ That is, one of you has reached the other through intercourse (al-dukhul). It is related from al-Zajjaj that it means seclusion (al-khalwa), but the first view is more sound.

﴿And they have taken from you a solemn covenant.﴾ This is the saying of the guardian (al-wali): "I have married her to you on the condition that you keep her in kindness or release her with goodness." It is also said that it is the meaning of what is narrated: "Fear Allah concerning women, for they are with you as captives (awan). You have taken them under the trust of Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful by the word of Allah." This is the solemn covenant.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And do not marry those women whom your fathers have married﴾. The people of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance) used to marry the wives of their fathers, so the Sharia came with the prohibition of this. ﴿Except what has already passed﴾, meaning: after what has already passed. Al-Mubarrad said: its meaning is: but what has passed in the Jahiliyyah, then it is forgiven.

﴿Indeed, it was an indecency and hatred﴾. It has been said that "kāna" (was) here is superfluous (ṣila), and its sense is: indeed it is an indecency, and this is like ﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force, nor to restrain them that you may take part of what you gave them, except﴾. A poet says:

(So how would it be if you saw the abodes of my people... and our neighbours who were noble?)

It has also been said: "kāna" is in its proper place, and its meaning is that in the Jahiliyyah they regarded it as an indecency and hatred, and they used to call the son of a man's father's wife "maqītan" (one who is hated). Al-Fāḥishah (indecency) is the most hideous act of disobedience. As for al-maqt (hatred), Abu 'Ubaydah said it is the intense hatred from Allah. Ibn 'Abbas said he meant hatred from the angels.

﴿And evil is the way﴾, meaning: wretched is the path."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Allah, exalted is He, forbade seven by lineage (nasab) and seven by marriage (mahr). The jurists (fuqaha') said: seven by lineage and seven by cause (sabab).

As for the seven by lineage: among them are the mothers, who are every woman to whom you are traced through birth, whether near or distant, whether or not there is a male or female between you and her. All of them are forbidden.

He said: ﴿and your daughters﴾. Among them are the daughters, who are every woman who is traced to you through birth, whether near or distant (in descent), whether or not there is a male or female between you and her. All of them are forbidden.

He said: ﴿and your sisters﴾. Among them are the sisters, who are every woman who is traced to the one to whom you are traced through birth. All of them are forbidden.

He said: ﴿and your paternal aunts﴾. Among them are the paternal aunts. The ʿamma (paternal aunt) is the sister of every man to whom you are traced through birth. All of them are forbidden, whether near or distant.

He said: ﴿and your maternal aunts﴾. Among them are the maternal aunts. The khala (maternal aunt) is the sister of every woman to whom you are traced through birth, whether near or distant.

He said: ﴿and the daughters of the brother and the daughters of the sister﴾. Among them are the daughters of the brother and the daughters of the sister, who are the daughter of everyone to whom you are traced, and to whom the one traced to you is traced. These are the seven by lineage.

As for the seven by cause: one of them is mentioned before this verse, in His saying: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women﴾. The second is in His saying: ﴿and your mothers who have nursed you﴾. The third: ﴿and your sisters through nursing﴾. There is no disagreement that the mother by nursing and the sister by nursing are forbidden to a man to marry. As for what is other than the mothers and sisters by nursing, it is also forbidden according to most scholars, based on his saying: "What is forbidden by lineage is forbidden by nursing."

Dawud and the Zahiri scholars said: what is other than the mothers and sisters by nursing is not forbidden, adhering to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.

He said: ﴿and the mothers of your wives﴾. The fourth: the mother of the wife is forbidden absolutely by the contract itself, according to the view of the majority. ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) is related by Khilas to have said: "The mother of the wife is not forbidden except after entering into the wife," based on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated marriage﴾. He said: so His saying ﴿of your wives with whom you have consummated marriage﴾ refers to both of them together. The first view is more correct.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: leave unspecified what Allah left unspecified, i.e., keep absolute what Allah made absolute. Also, His saying ﴿and the mothers of your wives﴾ is independent in itself and its ruling is complete, so it needs no specification. Also, if His saying "and the mothers of your wives from your wives with whom you have consummated marriage" were read with this restriction, it would be an impropriety in speech, and it is not fitting for the speech of Allah, which is the most eloquent kind of speech.

He said: ﴿and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated marriage﴾.

The fifth: the stepdaughter (rabiba), who is the daughter of the wife. She was called rabiba because the husband typically raises her in his care (yarubbuha fi hujrihi) in most cases. She is forbidden after consummation with the wife, whether she is in his guardianship or in the guardianship of someone else.

Dawud said: the prohibition is restricted to the one in his guardianship, based on His saying: ﴿and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship﴾. This is not sound, because the statement came out in the usual (majority) manner.

﴿And if you have not consummated marriage with them, there is no blame upon you﴾, meaning: in marrying them.

He said: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾. The sixth: the wife of the son (halilat al-ibn), and she is forbidden. She was called halila because she and the son share one bed; it is said that she lawfully unlocks the son's garment and the son lawfully unlocks hers; and it is said she was called halila because she is lawful to him.

His saying ﴿who are from your loins﴾ is restricted by "loins" only, even though the wife of a grandson is also forbidden, to make clear that the wife of an adopted son is lawful. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Zaynab bint Jahsh, the wife of Zayd ibn Harithah, and he had adopted Zayd, until ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said: "Look at this man, how he pounced upon his son's wife and married her." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾, for that reason.

﴿And that you combine two sisters, except what has already passed﴾. The seventh: combining two sisters is forbidden by marriage, and likewise by intercourse through ownership of the right hand (slave concubinage). The people of the Zahir said: combining them is forbidden only in marriage, because the verse concerns prohibition by marriage. ʿUthman said: "One verse forbade it and another made it lawful. The verse of prohibition is this one; the verse of permission is His saying: ﴿except what your right hands possess﴾." ﴿Except what has already passed﴾, i.e., after what has passed, and we have [explained it to you]. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the married women among the women﴾, meaning: those who have husbands. ﴿Except what your right hands possess﴾: they differed concerning it. ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means, except what your right hands possess from captives or from Awtas (a place), and the verse was revealed concerning it. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: "When the Messenger of Allah took captives at Awtas, the men fled, so the Muslims were reluctant to have intercourse with the women whose husbands were (still) alive; so the verse was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah permitted intercourse with them."

Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: His saying ﴿except what your right hands possess﴾ means that a man sells a married slave-girl, so the separation occurs between her and her husband, it becomes lawful for the buyer to have intercourse with her, and her sale is a divorce for her.

And there is said: the meaning of the verse, ﴿And the married women among women﴾, means: those who have husbands, with whom enjoyment is forbidden, ﴿except what your right hands possess﴾ from their dower, so enjoyment of it is lawful. Thus it is as if He forbade enjoyment of some of them and permitted enjoyment of their dower.

﴿The decree of Allah upon you﴾, i.e., Allah has made it obligatory upon you. It is also read: "Kitab Allah alaykum" (kutiba Allahu alaykum), i.e., Allah has made it obligatory upon you. ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾, meaning: Allah has made lawful for you. It is also read: "uhilla lakum" (with a damma on the alif), in keeping with the construction of His saying: (﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers﴾ ... that you seek [them] with your wealth). It is said: the making lawful (ihlal) is by seeking with wealth, and in it is evidence that obtaining intimacy (istihlal al-bud') is not free of a consideration (iwad). ﴿Chaste, not fornicating﴾, i.e., married, modest, ﴿not fornicators﴾, not committing zina, derived from safh al-ma' (pouring out water), which is pouring, and from it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

(And my healing is tears, if I pour them out... so is there any means at the trace of a deserted abode?) i.e., I poured them.

﴿So whoever you enjoy from them﴾. It is said: he meant by it: whoever you enjoy from them through marriage, ﴿give them their wages as an obligation﴾, i.e., their dowers. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the well-known mut'ah.

Mut'ah (temporary marriage) was lawful at the beginning of Islam, and its form was that a man would say to a woman: "I have hired you" or "I have contracted with you for me to enjoy you for ten days for such-and-such," and this was lawful, then it was abrogated. Ibn 'Abbas used to issue rulings permitting it, but the correct view is that it is abrogated.

'Ali and al-Rabi' narrated from Sabrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he forbade the marriage of mut'ah.

'Ali said to Ibn 'Abbas: "You are a bewildered man; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the marriage of mut'ah." It is said that Ibn 'Abbas retracted his permission of mut'ah and repented. Some of the early scholars said: "Had 'Umar not forbidden mut'ah, no one would have committed zina in the world."

﴿And there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾. Whoever understands what precedes as referring to mut'ah says: the meaning here is that the man may increase the dower and the woman may increase the term. Whoever understands that as referring to enjoyment through marriage says: the meaning of His saying ﴿there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree upon﴾ is: such as remission (ibra') and exchanging for the dower. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing, Wise﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 25:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford (ṭawlan) to marry free believing women, then let him marry from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾. Mujahid said: "al-ṭawl" means abundance and wealth.

The root of ṭawl is excess (faḍl), and from it comes ṭawl (height), meaning excess in stature. It is also said: "lā ṭāʾil taḥtahu," meaning there is no substance beneath it, i.e., no meaning in it.

The meaning of the verse is: whoever is unable to provide the bridal gift (mahr) of a free believing woman, let him marry a believing slave woman. This indicates that marrying a slave woman who is a People of the Book is invalid.

Al-Shaʿbi said: marrying a slave woman while being able to pay the mahr of a free woman is forbidden, like carrion and blood. ʿAṭāʾ said: ṭawl is desire (hawā), and the meaning of the verse is: whoever among them cannot restrain his desire to marry a free woman, such as one who desires a slave woman rather than a free woman, let him marry a slave woman. On this view, marrying a slave woman is permissible even if one is able to pay the mahr of a free woman. Al-fatā means the male slave and al-fatāh means the female slave, so the words ﴿from your believing young women﴾ mean: from your female slaves.

﴿And Allah is most knowing of your faith﴾, meaning: do not probe into the inner state of faith, but take by the outward appearance of faith, for Allah knows best your faith. ﴿Some of you are from others﴾, meaning: you all originate from one soul, so do not disdain marrying slave women. It is also said that the meaning is: some of you are brothers to others.

﴿So marry them﴾, meaning the slave women, ﴿with the permission of their people﴾, meaning the permission of their masters, ﴿and give them their wages﴾, meaning their bridal gifts, ﴿in a reasonable manner, as chaste women﴾, meaning: chaste through marriage, ﴿not unlawful sexual partners﴾, meaning: not fornicators, ﴿nor taking secret lovers﴾. Al-musāfiḥa (the fornicator) is the one who allows herself to everyone; al-Ḥasan said: al-musāfiḥa is the woman who follows whoever takes shelter with her. Dhāt al-akhdān (the one who takes secret lovers) is the one who keeps company with a single lover. The Arabs used to forbid the first and permit the second.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when they are married (uḥṣina)﴾. Ibn Masʿud said: "when they embrace Islam." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "when they marry." It is also recited as "uḥṣina" with the alif vowelled with a ḍamma, meaning: they are married off.

﴿And if they commit immorality, then for them is half the punishment of free women﴾. The meaning of the verse according to the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, which is the most sound, is that when slave women marry and become thayyib (previously married), ﴿then for them is half﴾ (﴿of the believing women. So whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then let him marry from what your right hands possess of your believing young women. And Allah is most knowing of your faith; some of you are from others. So marry them with the permission of their people and give them their wages in a reasonable manner, as chaste women, not unlawful sexual partners nor taking secret lovers,﴾ of what is for the free women), meaning: the free women, ﴿of the punishment﴾, meaning: of the punishment of the prescribed penalty (ḥadd). The prescribed penalty for free women is either by flogging or by stoning, and stoning cannot be halved, so what is intended is the halving of the flogging. Some scholars held that if a virgin slave woman commits fornication, there is no ḥadd upon her, based on the apparent wording of this verse, but this is not sound.

Al-Zuhri said: the ḥadd for a married slave woman is established by this verse, and the ḥadd for a virgin slave woman is established by the Sunnah, and the well-known Sunnah on this is his saying: "If the slave woman of one of you commits fornication, let him flog her."

﴿That is for whoever among you fears hardship (al-ʿanat)﴾. Al-ʿanat means fornication, though it may also mean hardship, as we have explained. ﴿But that you be patient is better for you﴾, meaning: refraining from marrying slave women, so that the child is not born a slave. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 26:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you﴾, meaning: that He may make clear to you. Similar to it is the saying of the poet:

(I wish to forget her memory, but it is as if Layla presents herself to me on every path)

Meaning: I wish that I might forget her memory.

His saying: ﴿to make clear to you﴾, i.e., to explain to you the rulings. ﴿And guide you﴾, i.e., direct you ﴿to the ways of those before you﴾, i.e., the paths of those before you, from among the prophets and the righteous. It is also said: from among the people of Musa and Isa, those who were guided by the truth; and that is because He prohibited for them what He prohibited for the Muslims of the aforementioned prohibited things. It is also said: its meaning is: and He guides you to the upright religion (al-millah al-hanifiyyah), the religion of Ibrahim. ﴿And turn to you in forgiveness﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "[It means] a change of decision from Allah" (bada'). Its meaning is: He enables you to repent. It is also said: He guides you to the path that calls you to repentance. ﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ of the interests of your affairs, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He arranges.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 27:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah desires to turn to you in forgiveness﴾ is as we have mentioned. ﴿But those who follow their desires desire that you should deviate [into] a tremendous deviation.﴾ Mujahid said: they are the fornicators. It was also said: by it is meant the Jews and the Christians. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: specifically the Jews, because they permitted marriage to a sister from the father's side.

﴿That you should deviate [into] a tremendous deviation.﴾ The tremendous deviation is that one commits an act without fearing Allah regarding it and without being mindful of people. It was also said: the tremendous deviation is by following desires.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 28:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Allah wishes to lighten [the burden] for you﴾, meaning: He wishes to make things easy for you. This religion has indeed been made easy. He (ﷺ) said: "I was sent with the tolerant, easy, upright (hanifiyyah) [religion]." And it was narrated: "with the upright (hanifiyyah), tolerant, easy [religion]." And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He removes from them their burden and the shackles that were upon them﴾, and ﴿man was created weak﴾. Tawus and Mujahid said: "And he was created weak regarding the matter of women; he cannot restrain himself from them." Waki' said: "His reason departs from him in their presence, so he is weak." Al-Zajjaj said: "His desire and his lust incline him."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 29:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾. Al-Suddi said: it refers to gambling (qimar), usury (riba), and the like. Others said: it refers to every invalid contract.

﴿Except that it be trade by your mutual consent﴾. It is read with a damma and with a fatha (tijaratun and tijarata), and we have already mentioned the reasoning behind the two readings in Surat al-Baqarah.

﴿By mutual consent among you﴾, meaning: with the good pleasure of your souls. ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾, meaning: do not let some of you kill others. Al-Hasan read ﴿wa la taqtulu anfusakum﴾ with the doubled qaf (taqtilu), for intensification.

It is also said: its meaning is, "And do not kill yourselves by consuming wealth unjustly." It is also said: it means the killing of a man of himself in the literal sense. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 30:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And whoever does that﴾, meaning what has preceded of the forbidden, ﴿in transgression and wrongdoing﴾. So ʿudwān (transgression) is exceeding the limit, and ẓulm (wrongdoing) is placing a thing in other than its proper place.

﴿Then We will cast him into the Fire﴾: We will make him enter a Fire, to be burned by it. ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾, meaning, easy.

It is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that he said: "We used to testify to the Fire for those who committed major sins, on the basis of these verses, until the Exalted's saying was revealed: ﴿And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, so we held back."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 31:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden﴾. The Messenger of God was asked, and it was said to him: "Which of the major sins is the greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival (nidd) to God while He is the One who created you." It was said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child out of fear that it will eat with you." It was said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Then he recited: ﴿And those who do not invoke with God another god, and do not kill the soul which God has forbidden except with right, and do not commit adultery﴾.

It is also narrated from the Messenger of God that he said: "The greatest of the major sins are: associating partners with God, disobedience to parents, fleeing from the battlefield, and false testimony, and false testimony." He had been reclining, then he sat up straight and said: "False testimony, false testimony." He kept repeating it until we said: "I wish he would be silent."

Ibn Mas'ud said: The major sins are what God, exalted is He, mentioned in this surah up to this verse: ﴿If you avoid major sins﴾.

Also from Ibn Mas'ud, he said: The major sins are four: associating partners with God, despair of the mercy of God, despairing of the spirit of God, and feeling secure from the plan of God.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The major sins are seven: associating partners with God, killing a soul without a soul being killed for, slandering a chaste woman, consuming usury (riba), consuming the property of an orphan, fleeing from the battlefield, and becoming a bedouin (ta'arrub) after the emigration (hijra), meaning: going to the abode of war (dar al-harb).

Ibn 'Umar said: The major sins are nine. He mentioned these seven and added two: the first is sorcery, and the second is violating the sanctity of the Sacred Precinct (ilhad fi al-haram) by inclination and wrongdoing.

Ibn 'Abbas was asked and it was said to him: "Are the major sins seven?" He said: "They are nearer to seventy than to seven."

Al-Mughira ibn Muqsim al-Dabbi said: Cursing Abu Bakr and 'Umar is among the major sins.

In sum: the major sins are every offence for which God, exalted is He, has threatened the Fire. Abu Salih said: A major sin is everything that necessitates a prescribed penalty (hadd). However, there is no major sin with seeking forgiveness, and no minor sin with persistence.

As for His saying: ﴿We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾. Al-Suddi said: By misdeeds (sayyi'at) He meant the minor sins. ﴿We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾ if You will; the will is implied in it. It is also narrated from the Messenger of God that he said: "From Friday to Friday, and the five prayers, are an expiation for what is between them, so long as the major sins are avoided."

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated from the Messenger of God that he said: "No Muslim is afflicted with fatigue or hardship, but that God expiates his sins because of it, even the thorn that pricks him." It is also said that by avoiding the major sins, minor sins are expiated. The doctrine of the People of the Sunna is that the expiation of minor sins is contingent upon God's will; so it is permissible that God pardons the major sins and takes to account for the minor sins, and it is permissible that a man avoids the major sins and is then held to account for the minor sins.

﴿And We will admit you to an honourable entrance﴾. It is read "mudkhalan" with a fatha on the mim: the mudkhal is Paradise. And the mudkhal with a damma on the mim is the act of entering, meaning: an honourable entering.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others.﴾ The occasion of revelation of the verse: it was narrated from Umm Salamah, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, men fight in battle but we do not fight, and they receive a share of the inheritance while our share is half of theirs. If only we were men, we would fight as they fight and take from the inheritance what they take." So there was revealed: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others.﴾ It was also said: the occasion of revelation was that the people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) did not give women any inheritance. When the verse was revealed giving women inheritance, and making the portion of the male equal to the share of two females, the women said: "If only we were men, we would take from the inheritance what they take." And the men said: "Just as we have been favoured over you in this world, we will be favoured over you in the Hereafter." So the verse was revealed.

Al-Farra' said: this is a prohibition of discipline and refinement (nahy ta'dib wa tahdhib). Others said: it is a prohibition of prohibition in the strict sense (nahy tahrim). ﴿For men there is a share of what they have earned﴾, meaning: of reward. ﴿And for women there is a share of what they have earned﴾, meaning: of reward. The meaning of the verse is that men and women are equal in reward in the Hereafter, even if men are favoured over women in this world; for the good deed is rewarded tenfold, and man and woman are equal in this. It was also said: its meaning is: for men there is a share of what they have earned from the matter of jihad, and for women there is a share of what they have earned from obedience to their husbands and guarding their chastity; that is, if the man has the excellence of jihad, the women have the excellence of obedience to their husbands and guarding their chastity.

﴿And ask Allah of His bounty.﴾ In this there is evidence that envy (hasad) is forbidden. Envy (hasad) is to wish for the removal of a blessing from its possessor and to wish it for oneself; and ghibta (wholesome desire to emulate) is to wish for oneself something like what one's companion has. So envy is forbidden, and ghibta is not objectionable. Then they differed about the meaning of "bounty" (fadl) here. Ibn 'Abbas said: "And ask Allah of His bounty" means of His provision (rizq).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: its meaning is: ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾, that is, of His worship ('ibadah). It was also said: it is the request for success (tawfiq) in obedience. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for every [one] We have made heirs (mawali)﴾. "For every one" means: of men and women, We have made heirs. Mujahid said: "mawali" here means the cousins (banu al-a'mam). And the poet said:

(Gently, O sons of our paternal uncles, gently, O our mawali; do not stir up between us what has been buried.)

It was also said: they are all the relatives. The meaning of the verse is: for every one We have made heirs who receive ﴿from what the parents and the near relatives leave﴾, and ﴿those with whom your oaths have bound you, give them their share﴾. "Aqadat" (bound), "'aqadat" (bound by a pact) and "halafat" (sworn allegiance) have one meaning, and it derives from alliance (hilf) and covenant ('ahd): it is when a man says to his companion, "My blood is your blood, my wealth is your wealth, you inherit from me and I inherit from you." In the pre-Islamic period inheritance was by alliance, and this was affirmed in Islam, and the ally had the sixth. Then this was abrogated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another﴾. It was also said: this concerns inheritance by adoption (tabanni), and it was established, then it was abrogated by ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has made one of them to excel the other, and because they spend of their wealth﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse: that the wife of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "My husband slapped me on the face, and this is its mark." He said: "Go and seek retaliation from him." Then the words of the Most High were revealed: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has made one of them to excel the other﴾, meaning: by way of discipline.

Al-Hasan said: When he said to her, "Go and seek retaliation from him," the words were revealed: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you﴾, meaning: do not judge before the ruling of Allah descends.

Al-qiwam and al-qayyim have one meaning, and al-qiwam is more emphatic: it is the one who stands over the interests and management, as the poet said:

(Allah is between me and her who maintains her affairs... she flees from me and I pursue her)

﴿because Allah has made one of them to excel the other﴾, meaning: men over women in intellect, knowledge and forbearance. ﴿and because they spend of their wealth﴾, meaning: by giving the dowry and maintenance.

﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient﴾, meaning: obedient; it is also said: those who pray. ﴿guarding in secret what Allah has guarded﴾, meaning: guarding their private parts in the absence of their husbands. ﴿what Allah has guarded﴾, meaning: what Allah has protected them with, through the husbands' charge to fulfil their rights of dowry and maintenance. It is also said that the meaning is: guarding in secret by the guarding of Allah. Abu Ja'far al-Madani read "bima hafiza Allah" with a fatha on the ha', meaning: by what Allah has preserved of their obedience and worship.

﴿As for those from whom you fear disobedience﴾: nushuz (disobedience) is discord (al-shiqaq). ﴿admonish them﴾, meaning: by frightening them with Allah and by admonition in speech. ﴿and forsake them in the beds﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is: turn your backs to them in the beds; that is, he turns his back to her on the bed and does not speak to her. It is also said: its meaning is that he withdraws from her to another bed.

﴿and strike them﴾, meaning: a striking that is not severe, a blow that causes no wound or fracture. 'Ata' said: a striking with a siwak or the like. ﴿Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them﴾, meaning: by pretexts and fault-finding. It is also said: do not burden them with your love, for the heart is not in their hands. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Most High, Most Great﴾, meaning: exalted above imposing on His servants what they cannot bear. In a report: "If it were permissible for one person to prostrate to another, I would have commanded the wife to prostrate to her husband, because of the rights he has over her."

It is also narrated in a marfu' report: "The best of women is she who, when you look at her, pleases you; when you command her, she obeys you; and when you are absent from her, she guards you."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 35:

﴿And if you fear a breach between the two﴾: it is nushuz (disobedience or discord between spouses). Abu Ubayda said: he meant by it, "If you are certain of a breach between them." So "fear" (khawf) here carries the meaning of certainty (yaqin), and from this is the saying of the poet:

("When I die, bury me beside a vine ... I fear that when I die I will not taste it") meaning: I am certain.

Al-Zajjaj rejected this from him and said: when the breach is certain, there is no point in sending the two arbiters. Rather, khawf here means zann (supposition, opinion), meaning: "If you suppose a breach between them." ﴿So send an arbiter from his family﴾, meaning from the husband's family, ﴿and an arbiter from her family﴾, meaning from the wife's family. ﴿If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring them into harmony. Indeed God is ever Knowing, Acquainted.﴾

Is it permissible for the two arbiters to separate the spouses? On this the early scholars (al-salaf) hold two opinions. The first: it is permissible to separate them, just as it is permissible to unite them without the husband's consent. It is narrated from Ali that he sent the two arbiters, and the husband said: "As for separation, no." Ali said: "No, until you accept the Book of God, the Exalted." Según this, the meaning of His words ﴿God will bring them into harmony﴾ is: God will bring the two arbiters into harmony regarding what is good, whether separation or union. The sound view, and the one on which the fatwa rests, is that separation is not permissible, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him﴾. It is narrated from Mu'adh that he said: "I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to me: 'O Mu'adh.' I said: 'Here I am at your service, and I am ready to obey you.' He said: 'Do you know what right Allah has over His servants?' I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'The right of Allah over His servants is that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him.' Then he said: 'O Mu'adh.' I said: 'Here I am at your service, and I am ready to obey you.' He said: 'Do you know what right the servants have over Allah?' I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'The right of the servants over Allah, if they do that, is that He admits them to Paradise and does not punish them.'"

﴿And be good to parents﴾, that is: be good to your parents. Among goodness to parents is gentleness of manner, not raising your voice above theirs, not snapping at them with a refusal, and being toward them like a humble slave toward his master. ﴿And to near kinsfolk﴾, that is: be good to near kinsfolk. ﴿And orphans and the needy {and the neighbour who is near of kin}﴾. Regarding it there are two opinions: one is that it is the neighbour who is also a relative; the second is that it is the neighbour whose house is nearby, the adjacent one. ﴿And the neighbour who is far away﴾. Regarding it there are two opinions: one is that it is the foreign, unrelated neighbour; the second is that it is the neighbour whose house is far off.

Reports concerning the right of the neighbour have been transmitted, among them: what is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Gabriel kept enjoining me concerning the neighbour until I thought he would make him an heir." He also said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not harm his neighbour." He said to his crier, until he cried out: "Beware, neighbours are forty houses, and whoever harms his neighbour does not truly believe in Allah."

'Aisha said to the Messenger of Allah: "I have two neighbours; to which of them should I send a gift?" He said: "To the one whose door is nearest to you." Thus the right of the near Muslim neighbour is threefold: the right of kinship, the right of Islam, and the right of neighbourhood; and the far Muslim neighbour has two rights: the right of Islam and the right of neighbourhood; and the protected (dhimmi) neighbour has one right, which is the right of neighbourhood.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the companion by your side﴾. 'Ali and Ibn Mas'ud said: it is the wife. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah and a group said: it is the companion on a journey. ﴿And the wayfarer﴾. Regarding it there are two opinions: one is that it is the one who keeps to the road; this was said by Ibn 'Abbas. Another said: it is the guest. He said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his guest." And he said: "Hospitality is three days; whatever exceeds that is charity."

﴿And what your right hands possess﴾, meaning: be good to the slaves. The last thing that was preserved from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is that he said: "The prayer, and what your right hands possess." That is: keep to the prayer, and the right of what your right hands possess.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-conceited and boastful﴾. Al-mukhtal (the self-conceited) is the arrogant one, and al-fakhur (the boastful) is one who takes pride in himself out of arrogance. A poet said:

(And if you were our lord, we would be ruled by you... and if you were given to vanity, then go away and be proud.)

That is: if you are inclined to vanity, then go away and be boastful. If it is asked: what is the meaning of this after these rulings? It is said: because a person may fall short in fulfilling the rights out of arrogance, so He forbade it. And in a report: "A man used to strut in a garment of his, so Allah caused the earth to swallow him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness upon the people﴾. It was said: it is general, applying to every miser in the world. And it was said that by it He meant the Jews and the Christians, who were miserly about the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they commanded their lowly ones to do the same. ﴿And conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾. ﴿We have prepared﴾, i.e., We have readied, ﴿for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 4, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people, and do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day﴾. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: They are the Jews and the Christians. Others said: They are the hypocrites.

﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion, then evil is the companion﴾, meaning: how evil a companion. The poet said:

(Do not ask about a man; look at his companion, for every companion is guided by the one he accompanies.)

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And what would it be upon them﴾, meaning: and what harm would there be upon them, ﴿if they had believed in Allah﴾. This is like a man who takes account of himself, so he looks at what is for him and what is against him. Allah the Exalted says, meaning: what would be upon them if they believed in Allah and the Last Day, ﴿and spent from what Allah has provided them. And Allah is ever Knowing of them﴾.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (even) the weight of an atom﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "mithqal namlah" (the weight of an ant). And the dharrah (atom) is the red ant (al-namlah al-hamra'). ﴿And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾. It was also recited: "yud'ifuha" (yudh'ifuha, with the doubled 'ayn), and the two have the same meaning. ﴿And gives from Himself a great reward﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 4, verse 41:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these people?﴾ Its meaning: "So how will the situation be when We bring from every nation a witness?" By "the witness from every nation" he means its prophet, and the witness of this nation is our Prophet (ﷺ).

The scholars differed over what their testimony is about. Some said: they bear witness to the conveyance of the message. Others said: they bear witness over their nations concerning their deeds.

They also differed over whether the Prophet (ﷺ) bears witness over one who did not see him. Some said: he only bears witness over those who saw him. The correct view is that he bears witness over all of them: over those who saw him and over those who did not see him.

It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Recite the Qur'an to me." I said: "How can I recite the Qur'an to you when it was revealed to you?" He said: "I want to hear it from someone other than myself." Ibn Mas'ud said: "So I began Surat al-Nisa'. When I reached His statement: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these people?﴾ the Messenger of Allah touched me with his hand and said: 'That is enough for you.' I looked at him, and his eyes were shedding tears."

In another narration: "When I recited this verse, the Messenger of Allah recited: ﴿And I was a witness over them while I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them.﴾"

In a third narration: "O Lord, this is for those whom I have seen; so how about those whom I have not seen?"

The original hadith is authentic.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 42:
