His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On that Day﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them﴾. It is also read: "that the earth were leveled over them" (la-tusawwa bihim al-ardu), meaning: that it would become level (tastawi). The meaning is that they wish they would become dust. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾. That is when the beasts are gathered, and then Allah, exalted is He, says to them: "Be dust," and they become dust. The disbelievers then wish that they would become like the beasts, dust. It was also said: they wish that ﴿you would be leveled with the earth. And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ — the earth would split open, and they would sink into it and perish, and the earth would be leveled over them, meaning: the earth would be over them.

﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾. If it is said: Here He has informed that they will not conceal from Allah any statement, and in another place He mentions their saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, so they have concealed. How then is the reconciliation? It is said: al-Hasan al-Basri said: this is in one station and that is in another station, and there are many stations on the Day of Resurrection. This is a well-known answer, cited by al-Qutaybi in Mushkil al-Qur'an. It was also said: its meaning is: they wish that they had not concealed from Allah any statement, for they say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ and similar things, and Allah then seals their mouths and makes their limbs speak, so they wish that they had not concealed from Allah any statement. This returns to His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieved wish﴾. It was also said: its meaning is: they are not able to conceal from Allah any statement.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ means: do not approach the place of prayer. ﴿While you are intoxicated﴾ — the more correct view, and the view of most of the exegetes, is that it means intoxication from drink. This is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Dahhak said: it means intoxication from sleep.

Intoxication (sukr) from drink is more severe than intoxication from sleep, since drink covers the intellect and understanding. The correct view is that it refers to intoxication from drink.

The occasion of the revelation of the verse is what has been related: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf prepared food and made drink, and invited a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah. They ate and drank until they became intoxicated. Then the time of Maghrib entered, and they stood for prayer, and they put one of them forward as imam. He recited the sura ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ and recited: "I worship what you worship, and you worship what I worship," reciting it this way to the end of the sura, omitting the "not" (la). So there was revealed His saying: ﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying﴾, meaning: until you can distinguish and understand what you are saying.

If it is asked: how did He address the intoxicated, when the intoxicated person is not addressed? It is answered: He meant by it, do not expose yourselves to intoxication at the times of prayer. So they would drink after the Fajr prayer and become sober by Zuhr, and they would drink after the late 'Isha' prayer and become sober by Fajr.

﴿Nor in a state of janabah, except those passing through [the mosque]﴾ means: do not approach the mosque, the place of prayer, while in a state of janabah, except those passing through. They differed concerning this. A group of the Successors, and it is the view of al-Shafi'i, said: it means passing through the mosque by a junub without sitting in it; so this was permitted. Some of them said that he performs tayammum for passing through, and then passes through if he has no choice but to pass through. The verse concerned some people of the Ansar whose house doors opened onto the mosque; so they were permitted to pass through by tayammum. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿nor in a state of janabah, except those passing through, until you have washed﴾.

﴿And if you are ill﴾ means: the ill with sores and wounds, and there are details concerning this that are mentioned in jurisprudence. ﴿Or on a journey﴾. The measure of travel is a day and a night's march. The people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y) said: three days' march. ﴿Or one of you comes from the toilet (al-ghaʾit)﴾. Al-Farra' said: its meaning is "or one of you comes from the ghaʾit," so that the sentence is sound. Al-Ghaʾit is the name for a depressed piece of land; since it was the custom of the Arabs to go to the ghaʾit for relieving themselves, the act of excretion was named ghaʾit by the name of the place.

﴿Or you have contacted women﴾. It is also read: "or you have touched (lamastum) women." 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas said: it means intercourse. Ibn 'Abbas said: indeed Allah is modest and generous; He refers to the ugly by the beautiful, so He referred to intercourse by touching. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Umar said: it is touching with the hand, and this is the view of al-Shafi'i. Whoever holds the first view says: tayammum for one in janabah is established by the explicit text of the Book; and whoever holds the second view says: tayammum for one in minor impurity is established by the Book, and for one in janabah is established by the Sunnah.

'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud said: the one in janabah may not perform tayammum at all, and they applied the verse to touching with the hand, and held to the apparent meaning of the verse.

The more correct view is that la-mas and mula-masa are one and the same. Some said: whoever reads ﴿or you have touched﴾ (awlamastum), there is in it evidence that the purity of both the toucher and the touched is nullified; and whoever reads (aw lamastum) there is in it evidence that the purity of the toucher alone is nullified.

﴿Then you do not find water, so perform tayammum﴾ means: aim for, and intend. Tayammum is intention (al-qasd). The poet said:

(I intended Qays, though between me and him lay much of the land, of a desert of rugged wastes)

﴿Clean earth﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: al-sa'id is dust, and this is the view of al-Shafi'i. Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-sa'id is what rises from the surface of the earth, and this is the choice of al-Zajjaj. Al-Zajjaj said: if one strikes his hand upon a solid, hard rock, tayammum is achieved, even if nothing clings to it. They cited His saying: ﴿clean earth, barren﴾, and meant by it the surface of the earth. The first view is more correct, because He said in another verse: ﴿wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾, meaning: from the sa'id; so this shows that it is dust, so that tayammum is with it. And His saying: ﴿clean (tayyiban)﴾ means: pure. Some said: lawful.

﴿Wipe your faces and your hands. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾. Al-'Afw is the one who makes things easy, and al-Ghafur is the one who covers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 44:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Book?﴾ If someone says: How can the Jews and Christians be called "People of the Book" (ahl al-kitab), when it is a term of praise, while they deserve blame?

It is said: He said that to establish the proof against them. And it is said: He named them thus according to their own claim that they are People of the Book.

﴿They purchase error﴾: because when they exchanged error for guidance, it is as if they purchased error with guidance, and every purchaser is one who exchanges.

{And they wish that you would stray from the way.

And Allah is most knowing of your enemies, and sufficient is Allah as a Protector, and sufficient is Allah as a Helper.

Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: be content with Allah as a protector, and be content with Him as a helper, so that the "bā'" (the letter bā', "with") remains in its proper place. Another [scholar] said: the "bā'" is extra (ṣila, a particle that adds no independent meaning), and its underlying sense is: "Allah suffices as a protector, and Allah suffices as a helper."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Among those who are Jews, there are those who distort words⦆ It has been said its implied construction is: "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, among those who are Jews, who distort words?" And it has been said its meaning is: "Among those who are Jews there is a group who distort words" ﴿from their places﴾ and they say ﴿We hear and we disobey﴾, because when they heard and did not obey, it is as if they said: "We hear and we disobey."

﴿And hear, without being made to hear﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: They would say to the Messenger of Allah: "Listen," then they would say among themselves: "May you not hear," and this is its meaning. Al-Hasan said: "Hear without being made to hear from you," meaning: hear from us, and we do not hear from you. ﴿And [say] "Ra'ina"﴾ They used to say this, intending by it the attribution of foolishness (ra'ana) to him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿distorting with their tongues and slandering the religion⦆, because their saying "Ra'ina" is from consideration (mura'a), so when they twisted it to foolishness, this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿distorting with their tongues⦆. And if they had said "We hear and we obey, and hear and look at us" (instead), i.e., look upon us, ﴿it would have been better for them and more upright⦆, i.e., more just. (But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little.) There are two views on this: one is that they do not believe except with a little faith, by which they do not deserve the name of belief; that is because they believe in Allah, the Last Day, and Moses. And it was said: its meaning is: they do not believe except a small group among them, and by this he meant 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and some people among them who embraced Islam.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 47:

﴿O you who have been given the Book, believe in what We have sent down﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿confirming what is with you﴾ of the Torah and the Gospel, ﴿before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs﴾. Al-tams (obliteration) means erasure. Its meaning is: before We obliterate the face and return it to the nape of the neck. It was also said that its meaning is: the growth of hair upon it, until it becomes like that of apes. It was also said: He will make their eyes be on the nape of the neck so that they walk backwards. It is related that when ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam heard this verse, he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with his hand over his face and embraced Islam, saying: "I feared that my face would be obliterated before I reached you." Likewise, Kaʿb al-Ahbar, when he heard this verse, embraced Islam in the time of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him).

If someone says: The Jews were threatened with obliteration if they did not submit, yet their faces were not obliterated, so how is that? It is said: This applied to a specific group of people who embraced Islam, namely ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, Thaʿlabah ibn Saʿid, Aws ibn Saʿid, al-Muhayriq, and a group; and had they not embraced Islam, they would have been obliterated.

It was also said: It refers to obliteration on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: By His words ﴿We obliterate faces﴾ He means: We leave them in misguidance; so the intended meaning is the obliteration of the heart. ﴿Or We curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath﴾, meaning: We will make them apes just as We made the people of the Sabbath apes. ﴿And the command of Allah is ever accomplished﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 48:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills﴾. It has been said: this is the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an. Ibn 'Umar said: "We used to pronounce that whoever committed the major sins would abide forever in the Fire, until this verse was revealed, and we held back. ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin﴾," meaning: he has invented a tremendous sin.

If someone says: Allah the Exalted has said, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with﴾, and He has said elsewhere, ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾. So how is the reconciliation between them?

It has been said: He meant by it, "Allah forgives all sins except shirk (associating partners with Allah)."

And in a report: when he (ﷺ) recited the Almighty's saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾, a man said, "And shirk, O Messenger of Allah?" So the Almighty revealed, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with﴾.

The Words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim themselves to be pure?﴾ The verse was revealed concerning Rifa'ah ibn Amr and Murhib ibn Zayd. They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with their children and said: "Is there any sin upon these?" He said: "No." They said: "We are like them: what we do by night is expiated for us by day, and what we do by day is expiated for us by night." So Allah revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim themselves to be pure? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills.﴾ That is, He purifies whom He wills.

﴿And they will not be wronged a fatil.﴾ That is: nothing will be diminished from their rewards if they submit (to Islam), nor from their burdens if they do not submit. Fatil, qitmir and naqir are three terms mentioned in the Qur'an. Fatil is the name for what is in the slit of the date-stone; qitmir is the name for the thin skin that covers the date-stone; and naqir is the name for the small pit on the back of the date-stone. This is the statement of Ibn Abbas. Others said: fatil is from the verb "fatl" (twisting), and it is the name for the dirt that accumulates between the two fingers when twisting. The poet said:

(You gather an army of thousands and raid, / Then you do not take from the enemy a fatil.)

This was said by al-Nabigha, and al-Azhari recited it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 50:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Look how they invent lies against Allah, and that is sufficient as a manifest sin﴾, i.e., by the lie (ﷺ)... 

Note: the passage as given ends with an unclosed parenthesis and does not contain the phrase "by the lie" in a way that clearly completes the sentence; the translation above follows the text exactly as provided.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 51:

Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in jibt (idols, sorcery) and taghut (false deities)? ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The jibt is sorcery, and the taghut is Satan." This is also the view of al-Shaʿbi. Qatadah said: "The jibt is Satan, and the taghut is the soothsayer (kahin)." And from Ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of al-Kalbi from him, that he said: "They are the names of two men from the Jews: the jibt is Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and the taghut is Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf." In another narration from Ibn ʿAbbas: "The jibt is the sorcerer in the Abyssinian language, and it was Arabicized." ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb mentioned, from Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "The taghut is everything that is worshipped besides Allah." He recited the words of the Exalted: ﴿And avoid the taghut, lest they worship it﴾. It was said to him: "What is the jibt?" He said: "I heard that it is the soothsayer."

﴿And they say to those who disbelieved, "These are better guided in the way than those who believed"﴾. This is the statement of a group of Jews who attended the pilgrimage season. The polytheists said to them: "Are we better in way, or Muhammad and his companions?" They said: "You are." This is evidence of the intense obstinacy of the Jews, in that they preferred the polytheists over the Muslims, despite their knowledge that they (the Jews) did not believe in any of the Books, whereas the Muslims believed in the earlier Books.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 52:

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed﴾ are the Jews. ﴿And whoever Allah curses, you will not find for him a helper﴾.

The Words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Or do they have a share of the dominion? Then they would not give the people even a speck (naqir)﴾. As for al-naqir, it is the name of that spot on the back of the date-stone, from which the palm tree grows. Regarding the verse there are two views. The first: it is an interrogative in the sense of denial and negation, meaning: they have no share of the dominion, for if the dominion were theirs, then they would not give the people even a speck. We have already mentioned the removal of dominion from the Jews. The second view: it is in the sense of affirmation, meaning: they have a share of the dominion, and by "dominion" he means wealth. Then, they would not give the people even a speck; this describes them with extreme stinginess, and this is by way of a parable, since among the Jews there are those who give wealth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ That is: rather, they envy. The scholars differed concerning who is meant by "the people" here. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid and a group said: it refers to Muhammad alone. Qatadah said: it refers to the Arabs; the Jews envied them for the sending of a Prophet from among them. There is a third view: it refers to Muhammad and his Companions. Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir said: "We are the people"; that is because they envied us.

When we take the first view, that it is Muhammad alone, they differed concerning the bounty mentioned in the verse, what it is. Some said: it is prophethood, which they envied the Messenger for. Others said: it is the permission of more than four wives, which the Jews envied him for, saying: "What is the matter with this man, that his concern is with marriage? He marries, and marries."

﴿And We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom﴾. By "the family of Abraham" he meant Dawud (David) and Sulayman (Solomon). "The Book" is the Book that was revealed to them. As for "wisdom" (al-hikmah), it was said: it is prophethood; and it was said: it is the Sunnah.

The meaning of the verse: if they envy the Messenger for the bounty he has been given, then let them envy the family of Abraham, for they were given the Book and wisdom. ﴿And We gave them a great kingdom﴾. They differed concerning the great kingdom. Whoever interprets the bounty as the permission of multiple wives interprets the great kingdom in that sense too. Dawud had ninety-nine wives, and Sulayman had a hundred wives. It was also said: Sulayman had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines. It was also said: our Prophet (ﷺ) was given the strength of seventy young men in sexual intercourse.

It was also said: the great kingdom is the kingdom of Sulayman. It was also said: it refers to their being supported with armies of angels.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Among them are those who believed in him﴾, meaning: in the Book. ﴿And among them are those who turned away from him﴾, i.e., turned away from it. It has also been said that its meaning is: among them are those who believed in Muhammad, and among them are those who turned away from him. ﴿And Hell suffices as a blazing fire.﴾ Al-sa'ir (the blazing fire) is the fire that has been kindled.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 56:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs – We will surely drive them into a Fire﴾, meaning: We will cast them into the Fire. It is also said: "sallā al-nār" (to roast in the fire, i.e., to be exposed to it) when one comes close to it. The poet describes a woman:

(She makes musk, aloeswood, and nadd ... a warming-place for her beside the brazier)

﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins, so that they may taste the punishment﴾. It is said: this verse was recited in the presence of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and Muʿadh ibn Jabal was with him. He said: "Their skins are changed every hour seventy times." ʿUmar said: "Thus I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say."

Al-Ḥasan said: "Every day seventy thousand times."

If it is asked: when their skins are changed, how is the other skin punished, not the one that was in the world? It is answered: the person is punished in the skin, not the skin itself. It is also said: the first skin is returned each time, but it is called "other skin," and such a usage is permissible; the Arabs say: "I made from my ring another ring," even though the second is a restoration of the first. And in a report: "The thickness of the skin of the disbeliever in the Fire is forty cubits, meaning its thickness and its molar teeth are like Mount Uhud, and the distance between his shoulders is a three-day journey."

And in the reports: "He will have a hundred skins, between every two skins a kind of punishment."

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾. ʿAzīz: Overpowering. Ḥakīm: in what He arranges.

The commentary says: ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. For them therein are purified spouses.﴾ We have already explained the meaning of all of this. ﴿And We will admit them to a shade, deep and extended.﴾ It is the shade that protects from heat and cold.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 58:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions. The first: what is meant is all trusts (amanat) in general. It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The one who betrayed a trust will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to him: 'Return the trust.' He will say: 'The world has gone; how can I return the trust?' Then the trust will appear to him in the Fire, and it will be said to him: 'Take the trust and return it.' He will come to take the trust, and he will fall into the Fire; then he will rise to take it, and he will fall into it forever."

In a report it is said that he (ﷺ) said: "Return the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you." And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "There is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness, and no religion for one who has no covenant."

The second opinion: it means entrusting the matter to the rulers (wulat), obeying them.

The third opinion, which is the view of the majority of the exegetes: what is meant is the returning of the keys of the Ka'bah.

The occasion of the revelation of the verse is what is narrated: "When the Messenger of Allah conquered Makkah, he took the key of the Ka'bah from 'Uthman ibn Talhah, opened the door, and entered the Ka'bah. When he came out, al-'Abbas said: 'May my father and mother be ransom for you, O Messenger of Allah, combine for me the custodianship (al-sidanah) and the provision of water (al-siqayah).' The Messenger of Allah intended to give the key to him, but there descended the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾. So the Messenger of Allah summoned 'Uthman ibn Talhah, gave him the key, and said: 'Take it, O sons of Talhah, as a perpetual and enduring possession; none will take it from you except a wrongdoer.'" It remained with 'Uthman during his lifetime, and when he died he gave it to his brother Shaybah, and it remains with the sons of Shaybah until the Hour.

﴿And when you judge between the people, to judge with justice﴾, i.e., with equity (al-qist), ﴿Indeed, excellent is that which Allah instructs you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 59:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾. They differed concerning "those in authority" (ulu al-amr). Ibn ʿAbbas and Jabir said, and this is the view of a group: they are the scholars (ʿulama') and the jurists (fuqaha'). Abu Hurayrah said: they are the rulers and the sultans. It was also said: they are the commanders of the expeditionary units (al-sarayا) whom the Messenger of Allah sent out in the battles. It is authentically related that the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him said: "Whoever disobeys my commander has disobeyed me, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah, and whoever obeys my commander has obeyed me, and whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah."

ʿIkrimah said: by it He meant Abu Bakr and ʿUmar.

﴿And if you disagree over anything, refer it back to Allah and the Messenger﴾. Al-tanazuʿ (dispute) is mutual contention; it is called tanazuʿ because each of the two opponents pulls (yanzaʿu) with a proof and a verse.

His saying: ﴿refer it back to Allah﴾ means: to the Book; and to the Messenger if he is alive, and to his sunnah if he has died.

Referring back to the Book and the Sunnah is obligatory, as long as there is something in the matter from the Book and the Sunnah. If there is not, then the method is ijtihad (independent reasoning). It is reported that Maslamah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik said to a man: "You have been commanded to obey us." The man said: "God has removed it from you, since He said: ﴿And if you disagree over anything, refer it back to Allah and the Messenger﴾, and you have disagreed." Maslamah said: "Where is Allah?" He said: "The Book." He said: "Where is the Messenger?" He said: "The Sunnah."

It was also said: referring back to Allah and the Messenger is that a person, concerning what he does not know, says: "Allah and His Messenger know best," and this is a good view. ﴿That is better and more excellent in outcome (ta'wil)﴾, meaning: better in its final result and consequence.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 60:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet desire to seek judgment from the transgressor (al-taghut), though they were commanded to reject it? And Satan intends to lead them far astray.﴾

There are two opinions concerning the verse. The first: it was revealed concerning a group of hypocrites, among them Khallas ibn al-Samit. They had a dispute with a group of Muslims. The Muslims said, "Let us seek judgment from the Messenger," and the hypocrites said, "Let us seek judgment from the soothsayers (al-kahana)."

The second opinion, which is the more sound: "A Jewish man disputed with a man from the hypocrites. The Jew said, 'Let us seek judgment from Abu al-Qasim,' knowing that he does not take bribery in judgment and rules with the truth. The hypocrite said, 'Let us seek judgment from Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.' So they went to the Prophet, and he ruled in favour of the Jew, and the judgment was in his favour. The hypocrite said, 'I am not content with his judgment. Let us seek judgment from Abu Bakr.' So they went to Abu Bakr, and he ruled in favour of the Jew in the same way as the Messenger of Allah had ruled. The hypocrite said, 'I am not content with his judgment. Let us seek judgment from Umar.' So they went to Umar, and Umar said, 'Have you both sought judgment from anyone else?' The Jew said, 'Yes, from Abu al-Qasim and from Abu Bakr, and they have both ruled in my favour, but he is not content.' Umar said, 'Stay where you are until I come out to you.' He entered the house, took up his sword, then came out and struck the neck of the hypocrite. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said, 'You are al-Faruq.'"

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you with [complete] aversion.﴾ This is as we have mentioned: the hypocrites were called to submit their disputes to the Messenger, but they turned away from him and sought judgment from the tyrant (al-taghut).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 62:

God the Exalted says: ﴿How then, when a calamity befalls them because of what their hands have sent before?﴾ It has been said: this refers to the hypocrites who sought judgment from the tyrant (al-taghut). As for His words, ﴿a calamity befalls them because of what their hands have sent before﴾, it has been said: it is the killing of that hypocrite by ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, for they came seeking his blood. It has also been said: it refers to all the hypocrites, and "calamity" means every calamity that befalls them in this world and the Hereafter.

God the Exalted says: How then will it be when a calamity befalls them because of what their hands have sent before? ﴿Then they come to you swearing by Allah, "We intended nothing but good (iḥsān) and reconciliation (tawfīq)."﴾ It has been said: iḥsān here is their showing kindness to one another. It has also been said: by iḥsān they meant bringing the matter closer to the truth, not issuing a judgment that would finalize the ruling.

As for tawfīq (reconciliation), it means agreement with the truth. It has been said: it means conciliation and bringing together the two disputants. The meaning of the verse is that the hypocrites swear, "We intended by seeking judgment from others than you nothing but good and reconciliation."

There is another view regarding the verse: that it concerns the hypocrites who swore at the mosque they built for harm, as is mentioned in Surah al-Tawbah: ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but the best."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 63:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts, contrary to what is on their tongues﴾. ﴿So turn away from them and admonish them﴾. If someone says: How can turning away and admonishing be combined, when Allah has commanded both?

It is said that its meaning is: turn away from punishing them, and admonish them.

And it is said that its meaning is: turn away from accepting their excuse, and admonish them. ﴿And speak to them about themselves a far-reaching word﴾. The far-reaching word (al-qawl al-baligh) is that which conveys to a person, through his tongue, the full reality of what is in his heart. It is also said that it is warning them by Allah the Exalted. And it is said that it is that he says: If you return to this, then your command is killing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 64:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed, by the leave of God﴾. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: His words ﴿except to be obeyed﴾ are a complete and self-contained statement, and His words ﴿by the leave of God﴾ are another statement, and its meaning is: by the knowledge of God and by the decree of God; that is, his obedience occurs by the leave of God.

﴿And if they﴾, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿when they wrong themselves﴾, meaning: by seeking judgment from the tyrant (al-taghut), ﴿came to you and sought God's forgiveness﴾. For they did not come seeking forgiveness; rather they came offering excuses with false pretexts.

As for His words ﴿and sought God's forgiveness﴾, meaning: they asked God for forgiveness, ﴿and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them﴾, meaning: the Messenger prayed for their forgiveness, ﴿they would have found God Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 65:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe﴾. His words ﴿But no﴾ are a rejection of the claim of the hypocrites and of their excuse. Then he begins with His words: ﴿by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe﴾. What is meant by this is complete faith (al-iman al-kamil), i.e., their faith will not be perfected, ﴿until they make you judge in what is disputed among them﴾, i.e., they differ. Al-isytijar (شجر, "dispute") means disagreement, and from it comes al-shajar (tree), because its branches intertwine with one another. The poet said:

(They are the judges, lords of generosity, and the nobles of the people, when the matter is disputed.) i.e., they differ. ﴿Then they find in themselves no discomfort (haraj) regarding what you have decided﴾, i.e., constriction. From it comes al-harajah (a thicket). It is related that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to some of the Arabs: "What is al-harajah among you?" He said: "It is a tree that is intertwined, and water does not reach it."

From this is the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He makes his breast constricted and tight (harajan)﴾, i.e., his path becomes so narrow that guidance cannot reach him. ﴿And submit in full submission﴾. The meaning of the verse is: their faith will not be perfected until they are content with your judgment and yield to you. It has been said: this is the most emphatic verse in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, in terms of warning.

They differed concerning the occasion of revelation of the verse. ʿAta' and Mujahid said: the verse concerns the hypocrites who sought judgment from the Taghut. ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, and a group said: "The verse was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar called Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, who was of the people of Badr, who disputed with al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam over water of land near the Prophet. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to al-Zubayr: 'Water your land, then send it to your neighbour.' The Ansari's land was lower than his. The Ansari said: 'Is he the son of your paternal aunt?' The face of the Prophet changed, and he said to al-Zubayr: 'Water your land and hold the water until it reaches the walls (al-jadr).'" In another narration: "until it reaches the two ankles (al-kaʿbayn), then release it to flow." The Prophet had been lenient toward al-Zubayr's right at the beginning of the matter; when the Ansari angered him, he gave al-Zubayr his full right. Both judgments were right. In the report, al-Zubayr said: "I think that the words of Allah, ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe﴾, were revealed concerning this."

It is also related that when the Jews heard of this, they said: "Look at the companions of Muhammad, how they oppose him. Moses rebuked us, and commanded us to kill ourselves, so we killed ourselves until the slain reached seventy thousand."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 66:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And had We prescribed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them.﴾ Its meaning: Had We prescribed for them, "Kill yourselves, or leave your homes," instead of what We commanded them with, namely obedience to the Messenger and submission to his judgment, ﴿they would not have done it, except a few of them.﴾ Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas said: "If the Messenger of Allah ordered me to kill myself, I would have killed myself." In a report: Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, and Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas were among that few. It is also narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) pointed to Abdullah ibn Rawahah and said to him: "You are among that few."

It is read as "illa qalilan minhum" (with the accusative). As for whoever reads it with the nominative (raf'), it is because it is coordinated (ma'tuf) with his saying ﴿they did it (ma fa'aluhu)﴾, and that is in the place of the nominative; its implied sense is: "they did not do it, except a small group of them who did it." As for whoever reads it with the accusative (nasb), it is by way of exception (istithna').

﴿And had they done what they were admonished with,﴾ meaning: obedience to the Messenger and contentment with his judgment, ﴿it would have been better for them and firmer in confirmation,﴾ meaning: in affirmation (tasdiq).
﴿And We would have given them from Us a great reward﴾. It is Paradise.
﴿And We would have guided them to a straight path﴾. It has been said: it is the Qur'an. And it has been said: it is Islam.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verses 69–70:

The saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever obeys God and the Messenger—those are with those upon whom God has bestowed favour﴾. The occasion of revelation (sabab nuzul) of this verse is what has been narrated: that some of the Companions of the Messenger of God said, "O Messenger of God, how will it be in Paradise? You are in the highest ranks, and we are below you. How shall we see you?" Then the verse was revealed. Al-Naqqash (d. 351 AH) mentioned in his tafsir that this questioner was Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Abd Rabbih al-Ansari.

It is also narrated that a man said to the Messenger of God, "You are dearer to me than my family, my wealth, and my children. When I am away from you, I am afflicted with something close to madness, out of love for you. So what will my state be with you in Paradise?" Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Those are with those upon whom God has bestowed favour from among the prophets﴾. It has been said: this means that the prophets will descend to them until they see them, not that they will be raised to their ranks. And it has been said: its meaning is that they will not miss seeing the prophets and sitting with them. His saying ﴿and the truthful ones (al-siddiqin)﴾ means the Companions of the Messenger of God; and al-siddiq is one who is intensely truthful. ﴿And the martyrs (al-shuhada')﴾ are those who were martyred on the Day of Uhud.

They differed about why they were called shuhada'. Some said: because they stood by the testimony of truth until they were killed. And it has been said: because their spirits witness Paradise immediately after being killed. ﴿And the righteous (al-salihin)﴾: the salih is one whose inner state and outward conduct are equal. ﴿And excellent are those as companions (rafiqan)﴾: the rafiq is singular in form, but here it carries the sense of the plural. ﴿That is the bounty from God, and God suffices as knower.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verses 69–70:

The saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever obeys God and the Messenger—those are with those upon whom God has bestowed favour﴾. The occasion of revelation (sabab nuzul) of this verse is what has been narrated: that some of the Companions of the Messenger of God said, "O Messenger of God, how will it be in Paradise? You are in the highest ranks, and we are below you. How shall we see you?" Then the verse was revealed. Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 71:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution﴾, meaning: your equipment. The ḥadhr (precaution) is that by which one guards against the enemy, such as equipment and weapons. (fanfiru thubāt) is the plural of thubah (a group). Ibn ʿAbbās said: "The thubah is what exceeds ten." Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "The thubah is the company (nafar)." Its meaning: go forth in groups, company after company, (or go forth all together).

This is evidence that jihad is an obligation of sufficiency (farḍ al-kifāyah) [a duty which, if fulfilled by some, lifts the obligation from the rest]. It has also been said that the verse was abrogated (mansūkhah) by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 72:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed among you is one who will certainly lag behind﴾, meaning: will certainly delay, and al-bat' (lagging, delay) is al-ta'khir (delaying).

It is said: this was about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. ﴿But if a misfortune strikes you﴾, meaning: by killing and wounding in the jihad, ﴿he says: "Allah has certainly blessed me, since I was not present among them as a witness."﴾, meaning: present.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 73:

﴿And if a bounty from Allah should reach you﴾ — that is, the spoils of war (al-ghanimah). ﴿He will surely say﴾ — with the lām in the accusative (li-yaqulanna); and in the irregular readings (al-shawadhdh) it is read with the lām in the nominative (raf'), though the meaning is the same. ﴿As if there had never been between you and him any affection﴾.

It has been said: in this verse there is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir), and its intended sense is: "If a calamity should befall you, he says: 'Allah has blessed me, since I was not present with them as a witness,' as if there had never been between you and him any affection," meaning a covenant (mu'aqadah) and pact (mu'ahadah) regarding jihad. It has also been said that by it he meant the affection of companionship (mawaddat al-suhbah).

Then he begins: ﴿And if a bounty from Allah should reach you, he will surely say, "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I could have achieved a great success."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the worldly life for the Hereafter﴾, i.e., who sell [it]. ﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or achieves victory, We will give him a great reward﴾. This is the meaning of His saying in Surat al-Tawba: ﴿They fight and are killed﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 75:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah﴾. He rebukes the Companions of the Messenger of Allah for abandoning fighting. ﴿And [for] the oppressed among men, women, and children﴾, who are those who had embraced Islam in Makkah and remained there under excuses, and some of whom were prevented from emigrating. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "I and my mother were among the oppressed."

Al-Azhari said: The meaning of the verse is: "You do not fight in the way of Allah, and in the way of the oppressed," by rescuing them from the hands of the polytheists; ﴿among men, women, and children who say, "Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers"﴾, and it is Makkah by the consensus of the exegetes; ﴿whose people are wrongdoers﴾, meaning, the polytheists among its people; ﴿and appoint for us from Yourself a protector﴾, meaning, one who will take charge of our affairs; ﴿and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾, meaning, one who will keep the enemy away from us. So Allah answered their supplication, until the Messenger of Allah conquered Makkah and appointed over it ʿAttab ibn Asid, who would give the oppressed their due and take retribution from the wrongdoer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 76:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut﴾. We have already explained the meaning of al-Taghut (the transgressor, i.e. any object of worship besides Allah). ﴿So fight the allies of Shaytan﴾, that is: the disbelievers. ﴿Indeed, the plot of Shaytan has always been weak﴾. It has been said that "it has always been weak" means that he cannot turn anyone away from Islam and guidance. It has also been said that he meant by it that his plot was weak on the day of Badr, when he saw the angels and feared that they would seize him, so he fled; thus his plot is weak in either of these two senses.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 77:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands and establish prayer and give zakat"?﴾ It is said: this was about a people who embraced Islam in Makkah, and the polytheists harmed them. So they said, "O Messenger of Allah, permit us to fight them." He said to them, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakat," for I have not been commanded to fight. Then, when he migrated to Madinah, he was commanded to fight, and they disliked fighting. It is said: they were those who embraced Islam and said that, among them: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, Qudamah ibn Maẓʿun, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi, and a group.

﴿But when fighting was prescribed for them,﴾ meaning: after the migration, ﴿behold, a party of them feared people as they should fear Allah or with even greater fear.﴾ That is: they feared people as they feared Allah, or with even greater fear. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They did not fear the command of Allah to fight; rather, that was the fear natural to human nature.

﴿And they said, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You would delay us to a near term."﴾ That is: "Why not delay us to a near term, so that we die by our own appointed times?" It is said: this was the statement of the hypocrites. It is also said: it was the statement of some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, who said it out of fear and cowardice, not out of belief. Some of them said: it was the statement of Talhah ibn ʿUbayd Allah; he said it out of fear, then he repented of it.

﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little.﴾ meaning: whatever you enjoy of this world is little. In the well-known report: "The world, compared to the Hereafter, is nothing but what one of you dips his finger into the sea; let him see what it returns with!" ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even as much as a thread.﴾ That is: nothing of their reward will be diminished, nor even the measure of a thread.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 78:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers built up high.﴾ Its meaning: wherever you are, death will come to you, even if you are within towers built up high. Al-buruj (towers) are fortresses. Al-Suddi said: they are white palaces in the sky. As for His saying ﴿mushayyadah (built up high)﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said, in the well-known report: it means well-constructed and lofty. 'Ikrimah said: al-mushayyadah means plastered with gypsum (jass), and al-shid is gypsum. Some of them said: al-mushayyad is the plastered, and al-mushayyadah is the raised. There is another report from Ibn 'Abbas: he meant: in towers of iron.

﴿And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah," and if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you."﴾ The good (hasanah) is fertility, and the evil (sayyi'ah) is drought. It is also said: the good is victory and triumph on the Day of Badr, and the evil is defeat and killing on the Day of Uhud. The meaning of the verse is: when good befalls the Muslims, the disbelievers say, "This is from Allah," and when evil befalls them they say, "This is from you," meaning: due to your ill omen. That is because when the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah, its people suffered some kind of hardship, and the Jews said: "We have not seen anyone more ill-omened than this man since he entered our lands; our prices have risen and our fruits have decreased." That was a trial for the Muslims. This is similar to what they said to Salih (peace be upon him): ﴿We see an omen in you and in those with you﴾, and in the story of Musa: ﴿they attributed ill omen to Musa and those with him﴾, and in Surah Ya-Sin: ﴿Indeed, we see an omen in you﴾.

﴿Say, "All of it is from Allah."﴾ That is: fertility, drought, victory, and defeat are all from Allah. ﴿So what is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?﴾ That is: what is wrong with them that they do not know any statement? Here, "hadith (statement)" means the Qur'an, i.e., they do not know the meanings of the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 79:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾. He means: whatever fertility (khisb) befalls you is from the bounty of Allah, and ﴿whatever evil befalls you﴾, that is, from drought (jadb), ﴿is from yourself﴾, that is, because of your sin.

Although the address is directed to the Messenger, what is meant by it is the community (ummah). This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned﴾. It has been said that its meaning is: whatever good befalls you, O human being, is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself; so the address is to every person. It has also been said that its meaning is: ﴿whatever good befalls you﴾, that is, of victory and triumph, is from the bounty of Allah; ﴿and whatever evil befalls you﴾, that is, of defeat and killing on the day of Uhud, ﴿is from yourself﴾, that is, because of the sin of your own opposition to the Prophet, as has already been mentioned.

If it is said: how is the combination of the two verses to be reconciled, given that He said in the first verse: ﴿Say: all is from Allah﴾? It is said: the meaning of the first verse is that fertility and drought, victory and defeat, all occur from Allah, ﴿to those to whom it was said: Restrain your hands, establish the prayer, and give the zakah. But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a party of them fear people as they should fear Allah or with greater fear, and they say: Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only...﴾ All of these occur from Allah. And the meaning of the second verse, ﴿and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, is: whatever evil befalls you is from Allah, but it is because of the sin of your own self, as a punishment for you.

Know that there is no basis at all in this verse for the Qadariyyah; for the verse concerns what befalls people of blessings and trials, not acts of obedience and disobedience. For if what was meant were what they imagined, He would have said: "Whatever good you attain is from Allah, and whatever evil you attain..."; since He said: ﴿whatever good befalls you﴾ and ﴿whatever evil befalls you﴾, this shows that He meant what befalls the servants of blessings and trials, not acts of obedience and disobedience. ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, on the authority of Mujahid, related that Ibn ʿAbbas recited: "And whatever evil befalls you is from yourself, and I have written it upon you." Likewise it is related from Ibn Masʿud that he recited in the same way, and this is well known from Ibn ʿAbbas, and it supports our view that what is meant is: because of the sin of your own self.

There is another view concerning the verse, with an implied element in it, and its estimate is: "What is the matter with these people that they hardly understand any statement?" They say: "Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself." So it is a quotation of the speech of the disbelievers. ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, and Allah suffices as a witness﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 80:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾. It is related that the Prophet said: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, the Exalted, and whoever loves me has loved Allah." The Jews said: "This man wants us to take him as a lord (rabb) and a compassionate one (hanan), just as the Christians took Jesus, son of Mary." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse in accordance with the saying of the Messenger. ﴿And whoever turns away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾, meaning: his affair is entrusted to Me.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 81:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they say, "Obedience."﴾ That is: the hypocrites say with the tongue, "We hear and obey" (mu-arana), for indeed your command is obedience. ﴿But when they go out from your presence, a group of them plot by night other than what you say.﴾ That is: they go out from your presence. Abu Razin said: "Bayyata" means "alafa" (they composed/arranged). Others said: "Bayyata" means "badala" (they changed). The more correct view is that it derives from tabyit, which is doing a thing at night (tabyit). It is said: "This is a matter planned (bayt) at night." It is said: that is, it was done at night. It is permissible to say of what is done by day as well: tabyiti, because an act done at night is only named tabyit because a person at night is freer to arrange his affair. On this meaning, it is permissible to say of what is done by day: tabyit. The poet said:

(They plotted their affair by night, and when they rose in the morning they were in a clamor)

The meaning of ﴿a group of them plot by night other than what you say﴾ is: they contradicted by night what they said by day. ﴿And Allah records what they plot by night﴾ That is: He counts and preserves it, so that they may be recompensed for it. It is also said: He commands the scribes so that they write it down. (So turn away from them.) Al-Dahhak said: its meaning is: do not inform about their names, and the Prophet (ﷺ) knew the hypocrites, yet he did not inform about their names. ﴿And put your trust in Allah, and Allah suffices as a Trustee﴾ That is: take Him as a Trustee.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 82:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ Tadabbur (deep reflection): looking into a matter to its end. It derives from dabar al-shay' (the end of a thing), i.e., its last part. In a report concerning the portents of the Hour: "And they will not come to the prayer except dabaran," meaning late (in its time). From this is also his saying: "Do not tadabaru," meaning: do not turn your backs to one another in enmity.

So His saying ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ means: do they not contemplate the Qur'an? ﴿And had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: there is no contradiction or inconsistency in the Qur'an; this is the meaning of the verse.

Al-Zajjaj said: whatever it reports of the unseen is entirely true; none of it is true while some of it is false. It was also said: its meaning is that all of it is eloquent and sound, with nothing in it that is base or corrupt.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 83:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When news of security or of fear comes to them, they spread it abroad﴾. He means: the hypocrites, when a matter and a report reached them concerning the expeditions (al-sariyya, small military detachments) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had dispatched. If it concerned security and victory, they concealed it and were sparing in reporting it; but if it concerned fear and defeat, they spread it abroad and embellished it.

In the verse there is an ellipsis (idmar), and its implied sense is: when news of security came to them, they were sparing in reporting it and concealed it; and when news of fear came to them, they spread it abroad. ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger﴾. It has been said that by His saying ﴿and if they had referred it﴾ He means: the weak among the Muslims who heard those reports from the hypocrites and said the same as they said. Then Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger﴾. It is also possible that what is intended in the speech is both the believers and the hypocrites: if they had referred it to the Messenger.

﴿And to those in authority among them﴾: meaning, to the commanders of the expeditions. ﴿Those among them who would know it would have known it from them (yastanbitunahu)﴾: meaning, if they had sought those reports from the commanders of the expeditions and entrusted the reporting of them to them, then those who wish to know it would have known it as it truly is. Istinbat (deduction, extraction) is the extraction of knowledge, and from it comes "al-nabt", which is a people who extract water. It has also been said: what is intended is the scholars, meaning: if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those among them who extract it (yastanbitunahu) would have known what should be concealed and what should be disclosed, meaning: the scholars.

﴿And had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few﴾. If someone says: how is "a few" excepted, when, had it not been for His grace, all would have followed Satan? It is said: the scholars differ concerning this. Al-Farra' said: this exception refers back to His saying ﴿they spread it abroad﴾, except for a few; and His saying ﴿And had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan﴾ is a complete statement. It has also been said: it refers back to His saying ﴿those among them who would know it﴾, and then He said ﴿And had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan﴾. It has also been said: it is according to its arrangement, and its meaning is: had it not been for what Allah bestowed upon you of clarification as to what should be done and what should be avoided, ﴿you would have followed Satan, except for a few﴾.

There is also a fourth opinion: that by "a few" He means a people who were guided to the truth before the sending of the Messenger and the revelation of the Qur'an, and who affirmed monotheism (tawhid). Such were Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, Waraqa ibn Nawfal, and a group. Concerning Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl it has been said: "Indeed, he will be raised as a nation apart."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 84:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿So fight in the way of God﴾ (fa-qatil fi sabil Allah). This is how it connects to what preceded it, His saying: ﴿And why do you not fight?﴾ When He rebuked them for abandoning fighting, He said to the Messenger: If these people do not fight, then you fight alone. ﴿You are not held responsible except for yourself. And urge the believers. Perhaps God will restrain the violence of those who disbelieve.﴾ He means: the punishment of those who disbelieve. "Perhaps" (asa) from God is binding, and what is meant by it is to make the believers hopeful. ﴿And God is greater in might﴾ i.e., greater in punishment, ﴿and greater in exemplary punishment.﴾ Tankil (exemplary punishment) derives from nakl, which means prevention, and from it comes nikal: it is what is done to a person so that others are prevented from doing the same.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 85:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share in it, and whoever intercedes with an evil intercession will have a burden of it.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: The good intercession is reconciling between people, and the evil intercession is walking about with tale-bearing (namimah) between people. It was also said: this applies to all intercessions. So the good intercession is that one says a good word by which good is attained, and the evil intercession is that one says an ugly word by which evil befalls.

His words ﴿will have a share in it﴾ mean: of its reward. And His words ﴿will have a burden of it﴾ mean: of its sin. The kifl (burden/portion) is the share. The Exalted said: ﴿He will give you a double portion (kiflayn) of His mercy﴾, meaning two shares.

Know that a person is rewarded for intercession even if he does not actually intercede, because the Exalted says ﴿whoever intercedes﴾ and does not say "whoever intercedes" in the sense of an actual act of intercession. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Intercede, and you will be rewarded, and Allah decrees through the tongue of His Prophet what He wills."

Know also that intercession is recommended in all rights except the limits (hudud) of Allah, the Exalted; for intercession is not permitted in them to cancel the prescribed punishment. He has said: "Whoever interceded concerning one of the limits of Allah, the Exalted, has opposed Allah in His dominion," meaning: he disputed with Him over His dominion.

﴿And Allah is ever Muqit over all things.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: al-muqit means the one who has power (al-muqtadir). The poet said:

(And one with a grudge whom I restrained my soul from, and I was over his harm a muqit.)

The second opinion from Ibn 'Abbas: al-muqit means the Guardian (al-hafiz). In a report: "It is sufficient sin for a person that he neglects those whom he sustains (yaqutuhu)," meaning: those whose sustenance (quwwah) he provides. In a narration: "man yuqit," meaning: those in his protection. There is also a third opinion: that Allah is Muqit over every living creature, meaning He delivers sustenance to it. This is the meaning of His words ﴿And Allah is ever over all things﴾, meaning: every living creature ﴿Muqit﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 86:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿When you are greeted with a greeting﴾. Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by "tahiyya" (greeting) here is the salam (greeting of peace). The original sense of tahiyya is a supplication for life (al-hayah), and in the Sharia it is an expression for salam, and salam is a supplication for safety (al-salamah). Tahiyya may also mean sovereignty and permanence, and from this comes "al-tahiyyat lillah" (all greetings are for Allah). The poet said:

(Everything that a young man attains, I have attained, except sovereignty.)

That is, except kingship. In the sense of salam they recited the poet's verse:

(We greet you, O Salma, so greet us back, and if the noble people of men are watered, then water us.)

﴿So return it with something better than it, or return it [equally]﴾. He meant by this: return the salam with something better than what was given, or return it as it was given. So if someone says, "As-salamu alayka" (peace be upon you), the recommended response is to say, "Wa alaykum as-salam wa rahmatullah" (and upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah). And if he says, "As-salamu alayka wa rahmatullah," you say, "Wa alaykum as-salam wa rahmatullah wa barakatuh," and this is the better response.

In a report: "A man came and greeted the Prophet, and he said: Wa alaykum as-salam wa rahmatullah. Then another entered and said: As-salamu alayka wa rahmatullah, and he said: Wa alaykum as-salam wa rahmatullah wa barakatuh. Then a third entered and said: As-salamu alayka wa rahmatullah wa barakatuh, and he said: Wa alaykum. He was asked about that, and he said, peace be upon him: The first and the second left something of the greeting, so I answered with the better; and the third did not leave anything of the greeting, so I returned it as it was given."

Know that salam is a sunnah, and returning the salam is an obligation (fard), but it is a communal obligation (fard kifayah): if the salam is given to a group and one of them returns it, the obligation falls from the rest. Likewise, giving salam is a communal sunnah: if a group is present and one of them gives salam, it suffices for the sunnah. Al-Hasan related as a mursal report from the Prophet that he said: "Salam is a sunnah and returning it is an obligation."

Some exegetes said: by tahiyya is meant gifts and presents, and His words ﴿so return it with something better than it﴾ mean the reward for the gift, which is a sunnah. "The Prophet, peace be upon him, used to accept gifts and reward for them." The more correct view is the first opinion.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Ever Reckoning﴾: that is, Muhasib (Reckoner). It was also said: Kafi (Sufficient). From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿A reward from your Lord, a sufficient gift﴾, that is, sufficient.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Allah—there is no god but Him. He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.﴾ The "lam" is the lam of oath (lam al-qasam), and its implied sense is: "By Allah, Allah will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection." The scholars differed about what He will gather them in. Some said: He will gather them in destruction and death until the Resurrection. Others said: He will gather them in the graves until the Resurrection.

The scholars also differed about why the Resurrection is called al-Qiyamah (the Standing up). Some said: because people will stand in it before the Lord of the worlds, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The Day when people will stand before the Lord of the worlds.﴾ It was also said: because people will stand in it for the reckoning. ﴿And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾ That is: in speech and report.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 88:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why then are you divided into two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾ The scholars differed regarding the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse, according to three opinions.

Zayd ibn Thabit said: This was about those who lagged behind from the Messenger of Allah on the day of Uhud. Some of the Companions said to the Messenger of Allah: "Pardon them, for they spoke the words of Islam." Others among them said: "Kill them, for they are hypocrites." So the verse was revealed: ﴿Why then are you divided into two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾ That is: What is the matter with you that you have split into two factions about them? He rebuked them for their disagreement among themselves, and He ruled that they were hypocrites.

Mujahid said: The verse concerns a group of people of Makkah who emigrated to Madinah and embraced Islam. Then they asked the Messenger of Allah for permission to return to Makkah, on the pretext that they had merchandise there. So they returned and apostatized. Some of his Companions said: "They are Muslims, because they spoke the words of Islam." Others said: "They have become hypocrites." Then the words of Allah, exalted is He, were revealed: ﴿Why then are you divided into two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾ Mujahid related this from Ibn Abbas.

The third opinion, which is the second narration from Ibn Abbas: the verse concerns a people among the polytheists who embraced Islam in Makkah, and who used to assist the polytheists and back them. The Companions disagreed about them into two groups. Then the words of Allah, exalted is He, were revealed: ﴿Why then are you divided into two groups concerning the hypocrites? And Allah has returned them [to their former state] for what they earned.﴾ Arkasahum (ﺃﺭﻛﺴﻬﻢ) and rakasahum (ﺭﻛﺴﻬﻢ) have the same meaning.

Ibn Mas'ud read: ﴿And Allah has rakasahum﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: He turned them upside down (nakkasahum). Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Its meaning is: He returned them, that is, to disbelief, for what they earned. From it comes al-riks (the refuse), because it was food which became dung.

﴿Do you want to guide those whom Allah has sent astray?﴾ That is: Do you want to guide to rightness those whom Allah has misguided? ﴿And whomever Allah sends astray﴾ That is: whomever He misguides, ﴿you will not find for him a way﴾ That is: a path to the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 89:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved﴾, meaning: those who returned to disbelief wish that you would return to disbelief, ﴿and then you would be equal﴾, meaning: in disbelief.

﴿So do not take from among them allies﴾, meaning: He forbade them from allying with them. ﴿until they emigrate in the way of Allah﴾, meaning: until they become Muslims. ﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning: in disbelief, ﴿then seize them﴾, meaning: take them captive. Here "al-akhdh" (seizing) means capture, and the captive is called "akhidh" (captive). ﴿And kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them an ally or a helper.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 90:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: its meaning is "except those who are affiliated with (yantasibuna ila) a people," and he cited in support the verse of the poet:

(When she is joined, she says to Bakr ibn Wa'il... and Bakr has taken her captive, while the noses are humbled)

Meaning: when that tribe is affiliated (with them).

But the scholars of the meanings (Ahl al-Ma'ani) rejected this from Abu 'Ubayda and said: this does not hold in the sense of this exception, which is a prohibition from killing, and the prohibition was not on account of affiliation, for the Prophet used to fight the polytheists of Quraysh even though they were of his lineage. Rather, the meaning of his saying ﴿Except those who join﴾ is: those who mix with and become connected to a people with whom there was a truce and covenant between them and the Prophet.

This refers to Hilal ibn 'Uwaymir al-Aslami and his people. God, exalted is He, had forbidden the killing of those who were connected to them, and who were under their protection. ﴿Or who come to you﴾: or who join a people who came to you for alliance and truce. ﴿Their breasts constrained﴾: their breasts were straitened, so their breasts were constricted from fighting alongside you, and from helping you to fight alongside their own people, because of the terror that God, exalted is He, had cast into their hearts. Al-Hasan recited it, and it is the reading of Ya'qub and Sahl, "hasirat sudooruhum" (ḥaṣirah ṣudūruhum) as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: their breasts being constricted. Al-Mubarrad said: "their breasts are constrained" is in the form of a supplication, like His saying: ﴿May God fight them﴾, as if God, exalted is He, were saying: "May their breasts be constrained against fighting you or fighting their own people," in the form of a supplication.

﴿And had God willed, He would have given them power over you﴾: the meaning of this is that God, exalted is He, is the One who cast terror into their hearts and restrained them from fighting you, until they came as covenanters. And had God willed, He would have given them power over you, ﴿so they would have fought you﴾; so do not fight them or those connected to them. ﴿But if they keep away from you and do not fight you, and offer you peace﴾, meaning: reconciliation, and submit and surrender, ﴿then God has not made for you any way against them﴾, meaning: any path against them by killing or fighting.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 91:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿You will find others who wish to be secure from you and secure from their own people﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: By this He meant Asad and Ghatafan. They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and embraced Islam; but when they returned to their people they said: "We believed in the scorpion and the beetle," and they went back to disbelief.

Qatadah said: By this He meant Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum. When he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "I am one of you," then he returned to his people and said: "I am one of you."

﴿Except those who reach a people between whom and you there is a treaty, or who come to you with hearts constrained from fighting you or fighting their own people. And had Allah willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they keep away from you and do not fight you, and offer you peace﴾

﴿They wish to be secure from you and secure from their own people﴾: that is, they wish to be safe from you and from their own people. ﴿Whenever they are returned to disorder, they are plunged back into it﴾: that is, whenever they are called to association (shirk), they enter into it.

﴿So if they do not keep away from you, and do not offer you peace, nor restrain their hands﴾: meaning submission and surrender (al-qiyadah wa al-istislam). ﴿Then seize them and kill them wherever you overtake them﴾: that is, take them captive and kill them wherever you find them. ﴿And those—We have given you clear authority over them﴾: a manifest proof to slay and fight them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 92:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by error.﴾ The occasion of revelation of the verse: it is narrated that 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah killed al-Harith ibn Yazid, and al-Harith used to harm 'Ayyash in the Jahiliyyah, until 'Ayyash embraced Islam. So he vowed that he would kill him whenever he got the chance. He gained power over al-Harith, and al-Harith had embraced Islam, but he (i.e. 'Ayyash) did not know of his Islam, so the verse was revealed: ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer.﴾ This is a prohibition of killing a believer absolutely. His saying ﴿except by error﴾ is an exception of the disconnected type (istithna' munqati'), and its meaning is: "but if it happens by error." Some of them said: "illa" here means "wa la" (and not), i.e. "and not by error," but "illa" with the meaning of "wa la" is not known in the speech of the Arabs. Moreover, it would imply a prohibition of killing by error, whereas error does not fall under command or prohibition. The first view is more correct. Then he mentioned the ruling on killing by error, saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer by error, then the freeing of a believing slave⁠ ﴾ — that is, free a believing slave. Then the scholars differed. Al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi and al-Nakha'i said: he intended by it a slave who has reached maturity, and a young slave does not suffice, even if he is a believer. 'Ata' said, and it is the view adopted by the jurists, that a young slave suffices.

﴿And a compensation paid to his family⁠ ﴾ — that is, hand over the blood-money (diyah) to his family. The apparent meaning of the verse implies that the blood-money for killing by error should be from the property of the killer, like the expiation (kaffarah). But we know from the Sunnah that the expiation is from the property of the killer, while the blood-money is upon the 'aqilah (the paternal kin who bear the liability).

His saying ﴿unless they remit it⁠ ﴾ — that is, unless they give it as charity. Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited it thus. The meaning of tasaddaq (giving as charity) is to waive the blood-money. ﴿If he was from a people hostile to you, and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave⁠ ﴾ — most of the exegetes, and it is the view of al-Hasan, Qatadah, Mujahid and a group, hold that what is meant is: "And if he was from the lineage of a people hostile to you, and he is a believer," meaning a believer who is in the abode of Islam while his relatives are in the abode of war, so he is killed by error. The one who killed him owes the expiation, and no blood-money, because if it were handed over to his relatives, they would strengthen themselves with it against the Muslims. The more correct view, which the jurists have recognized, is that what is meant is a believer who embraced Islam in the abode of war, and whom someone killed without knowing of his Islam. The obligation in this case is the expiation, not the blood-money.

﴿And if he was from a people between you and them is a covenant⁠ ﴾ — this refers to the protected people (ahl al-dhimmah) and those with treaties. ﴿Then a compensation paid to his family⁠ ﴾ — that is, according to the measure on which there is disagreement. ﴿And the freeing of a believing slave. But whoever does not find (one), then fasting for two consecutive months, as a repentance from Allah⁠ ﴾ — that is, so that they may repent to Allah. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing, Wise⁠ ﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 4, verse 93:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾. The verse was revealed concerning Muqayyis ibn Dababa al-Laythi. He embraced Islam, and so did his brother Hisham. Then he found his brother killed among the Banu al-Najjar, so he came to the Prophet about it. The Prophet sent a man with him. The two of them went to the Banu al-Najjar, and he ordered them to hand over to him the killer of his brother, or to pay the blood-money (diya). They came to them and conveyed the message. They said: "We hear and obey the Messenger of God. By God, we do not know the killer." They then delivered to him one hundred camels as blood-money. When the two returned, Muqayyis attacked and killed the al-Fihri, drove off the camels, joined Makkah, and apostatised. He recited poetry:

(I killed the al-Fihri in exchange, and I carried his blood-money,
the chiefs of the Banu al-Najjar, the lords of Fari'.)

(I attained my vengeance and lay down wealthy,
and I was the first to return to the idols.)

So the verse was revealed concerning him. He is the one whom the Prophet ordered to be killed. On the day of the conquest of Makkah, the group he had been designated for was sent to kill him, and he was killed while clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah.

As for His words ﴿and whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾: according to most scholars, intentional killing (al-qatl al-'amd) is that which occurs by any means intended to kill. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Tawus said: intentional killing occurs only with iron.

﴿His recompense is Hell, abiding therein; and God will be angry with him and curse him﴾, meaning: He will expel him from mercy. ﴿And He has prepared for him a great punishment.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: the verse is Madinan (revealed in Madinah), and nothing has abrogated it. He used to say: there is no repentance for one who kills a believer. He was asked about his repentance and said: "How can he have repentance?" It was said to him: "Did not God the Exalted say: ﴿And they do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right, nor do they commit unlawful sexual intercourse; and whoever does that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation, except one who repents﴾?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "That is a Makkan verse, and this is a Madinan verse, not abrogated by anything until the Messenger of God passed away."

Zayd ibn Thabit said: the severe (al-shadidah) came six months after the lenient (al-hayyinah). By the lenient he meant the verse of al-Furqan, and by the severe this verse.

Humayd narrated from Anas, from the Prophet, that he said: "God has refused that there be repentance for the killer of a believer." And in a report from the Prophet: "The killing of a believer is greater in the sight of God than the disappearance of the world."

The more correct view, held by most scholars, and the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah), is that the killer of a believer by intention has repentance. The evidence for this is His words: ﴿And indeed I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes﴾, and His words: ﴿And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. Also, intentional killing is not more grave than disbelief, and disbelief is forgiven by repentance, so killing is more deserving of forgiveness. As for what was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, it is meant as a strict emphasis and an intensification of the warning against killing. It is like what was narrated from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, that he said: if one has not killed, it is said to him: "There is no repentance for you," to prevent him from killing; and if he has killed, it is said to him: "There is repentance for you, until he repents."

It is also related that a man came to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him: "Does the killer of a believer have repentance?"
