He said: "No." Then another man came and asked him about that, and he said: "Yes, he has repentance." It was said to him about this, and he said: "The first had not killed, so I prevented him from killing. The second had killed, so I guided him to repentance."

Know that there is no basis in this verse for those who say that the people of major sins among the Muslims abide eternally in the Fire. For if we consider the occasion of revelation of the verse, it was revealed concerning a disbelieving killer, as we have shown. It was also said that it concerns one who kills while considering it lawful. The best position is what Abu Salih said: the meaning of His words ﴿His recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾ is "if He recompenses." We say accordingly: if God recompenses him with that, abiding eternally, then that is his recompense. But He may not recompense him, and He has promised not to recompense and to forgive whom He wills, and He does not break His promise.

It is related from Quraysh ibn Anas, may God have mercy on him, that he said: "I was in a gathering in which was 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd, and he said: 'If God were to say to me on the Day of Resurrection: Why did you say that the intentional killer is eternal in the Fire? I would say to Him: You are the one who said: ﴿His recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾.'" Quraysh said: "I was the youngest of the people, so I said to him: 'Tell me, if God said to you: Did you not say ﴿And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾? From where did you know that I did not will to forgive the killer?'" Then he was silent and could not answer.

It is related that 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd came to Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala', may God have mercy on him, and said to him: "Does God break His promise?" He said: "No." He said: "Did not God say: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾? So I hold to this, because He does not break His promise." Abu 'Amr said: "From ignorance of the language have you come, O Abu 'Uthman. The Arabs do not regard failing to carry out a threat as breaking a promise, or as a blameworthy act. That applies only to failing to fulfil a promise." He recited to him the words of the poet about himself:

(When I threaten him, I promise him,
I break my threat and fulfil my promise.)

So he praised himself for breaking a threat. Another said:

(When he promises a benefit, he fulfils his promise,
and if he threatens harm, pardon prevents it.)

So God may break a threat, but He does not break a promise.

O you who believe! When you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate carefully, and do not say to anyone who offers you peace, "You are not a believer," seeking the goods of this worldly life. With Allah are abundant spoils. Such were you before, but Allah conferred His favour upon you, so investigate carefully. Indeed Allah is ever Aware of what you do.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 94:

The words of the Most High: ﴿O you who believe! When you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾ means: when you travel in the cause of Allah, meaning: in raiding (al-ghazw). ﴿Investigate carefully﴾ and it is read: "fa-tathabbatu" (be steadfast and firm). Both readings mean: abandon haste.

And in a report: "Deliberation is from Allah, and haste is from Satan." ﴿Investigate carefully, and do not say to anyone who offers you peace (al-salam): "You are not a believer."﴾ It is read "ilaykum al-salam" and it is read "ilaykum al-silm." Al-salam is the well-known greeting of peace (al-taslim). Al-silm means submission and surrender; al-silm also means reconciliation (al-sulh). Abu Ja'far al-Madani Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa' read: "last mu'minan," from security (al-aman). ﴿Seeking the goods of the life of this world﴾ meaning: you seek the worldly life. In the reports: "The world is a present provision, from which the righteous and the wicked both eat, and the Hereafter is a true promise, in which a powerful King decides."

(﴿O you who believe! When you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate carefully, and do not say to anyone who offers you peace, "You are not a believer," seeking the goods of this worldly life. With Allah are abundant spoils. Such were you before, but Allah conferred His favour upon you, so investigate carefully. Indeed Allah is ever Aware of what you do.﴾) With Allah are abundant spoils: meaning, abundant booty. ﴿Such were you before, but Allah conferred His favour upon you﴾ meaning: Allah bestowed His grace upon you. There are two views on this. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: its meaning is, "Such were you before, concealing your faith, but Allah conferred upon you the favour of manifesting it." Qatadah said: its meaning is, "Such were you before, in misguidance, but Allah conferred upon you the favour of guidance." ﴿So investigate carefully﴾ is a repetition for emphasis. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Aware of what you do﴾.

The occasion of revelation of the verse is what is related: that the Prophet (ﷺ) sent a detachment (sariyyah), and they met a man called Mirdas ibn 'Amr from Fadak, who had a few small herds. When he sensed the detachment, he withdrew with them to the mountain. Then he approached them and said, "Peace be upon you, I am a believer." Usamah ibn Zayd hastened toward him, and he was saying, "There is no god but Allah," and he killed him and took his spoils and the herds that were his. When they returned to the Prophet, he said to Usamah, "Did you kill a man who says, 'There is no god but Allah'?" He said, "He only professed Islam seeking refuge." He said, "He only professed Islam to secure his life and property." The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "Why did you not split open his heart?" Usamah said, "Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "How will you fare with 'There is no god but Allah' on the Day of Resurrection?" He said, "Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "How will it be with 'There is no god but Allah' on the Day of Resurrection?" He repeated it thus until he had said it three times. Then the verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿And do not say to anyone who offers you peace﴾. And because that man had greeted them and submitted to them. ﴿"You are not a believer," seeking the goods of this worldly life﴾ meaning: by killing him you seek the herds that he had.

In another narration, the Prophet asked forgiveness for Usamah and commanded him to free a slave. Usamah was among the eminent Companions, and he lived until the time of 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him). 'Ali invited him to fight alongside him in the battles, and he said to 'Ali: "You are dearer to me than anyone, and if I were to fight the Muslims alongside anyone, I would fight alongside you. But since I heard the Messenger of Allah say to me, 'How will it be with "There is no god but Allah" on the Day of Resurrection?', I have refrained from fighting. If you give me a sword that distinguishes the Muslim from the disbeliever, I will fight." So 'Ali left him.

Among those who withdrew from both parties were Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Zayd ibn Thabit, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them all.

It is also said: the slayer of the owner of the herds was al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr al-Kindi, son of al-Aswad. This is the well-known view regarding the occasion of revelation. There is another view concerning the verse: "It was revealed concerning Muhallam ibn Jaththamah al-Laythi, who killed a man while he was saying, 'There is no god but Allah.' Then he came to the Prophet and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me.' He said, 'May Allah not forgive you.' He stood up weeping and left. When he died he was buried in the earth, but the earth expelled him. Then he was buried and the earth expelled him; then he was buried and the earth expelled him - thus three times. So the Prophet commanded that stones be cast upon him. He said, 'Indeed the earth would accept those worse than him' - meaning Muhallam - 'but Allah, the Most High, wanted to show you the sign.'"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 95:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than those who have a [legitimate] excuse.﴾ Know that what was first revealed of this verse was His saying: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives." Zayd ibn Thabit said: "The Prophet was dictating this verse while his thigh was upon my thigh. Then Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum entered and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I am a blind man, and if I were able to fight, I would have fought alongside you.' Then the Messenger of Allah was overtaken by revelation, and his thigh became so heavy upon my thigh that I feared it would crush it. When it lifted from him, he said to me: 'Write: ﴿other than those who have a [legitimate] excuse.﴾' So this phrase was revealed concerning Ibn Umm Maktum, who was blind and one of those with a legitimate excuse."

His saying ﴿other than those who have a [legitimate] excuse﴾ is recited in several ways. "Ghayr" with a raised (ḍammah) "r" [ghayru], and its interpretation is: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] who are other than those with a legitimate excuse." It is also recited with a fatḥah on the "r" [ghayra], as an exception (istithnā'), meaning: "except those with a legitimate excuse." It was also said that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: in the state of health and the absence of harm, as if he said: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers while healthy." This is the more well-known of the two readings. The Prophet also recited it as "ghayri" with a kasrah on the "r," meaning: among the believers, other than those with a legitimate excuse.

﴿Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit [at home] by a degree.﴾ By "those who sit [at home]" here he means those with a legitimate excuse; the strivers are preferred over them by a degree, because the strivers actually engaged in jihad together with the intention, whereas those with a legitimate excuse had the intention of jihad but did not actually take part, so they fall short of them by a degree. ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best [reward]﴾, meaning Paradise. ﴿But Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit [at home] with a great reward.﴾ By "those who sit [at home]" here he means those other than those with a legitimate excuse; Allah has preferred the strivers over them with a great reward.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 96:

﴿Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy﴾ Ibn Muhayriz said: "They are seventy degrees, the distance between each two degrees being the gallop of a trained horse for seventy years." And in a report: "In Paradise there are a hundred degrees, the distance between each two degrees being what lies between the heaven and the earth, which Allah has prepared for those who strive in His way." It was also said: by the degrees he meant Islam, emigration (hijrah), jihad, and martyrdom in jihad, and the strivers obtained those degrees. ﴿And Allah is ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 97:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death﴾. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar al-Nahwī (the grammarian) read "tatawaffāhum" with two tāʾs. The well-known reading is "tawaffāhum," and its original form is "tatawaffāhum," in which one of the two tāʾs was assimilated (idghām) for ease (takhfīf) according to the well-known recitation. If someone says: why did He say "the angels take them in death," when the one who takes in death is a single angel, as He said: ﴿Say: The angel of death will take you in death﴾? It is said: He mentioned it in the plural form while meaning the singular, and such usage is common in the speech of the Arabs. It is also said: the Angel of Death has helpers, so perhaps He meant him together with his helpers; for this reason it was mentioned in the plural form.

ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the verse concerns people who embraced Islam in Makkah before the Hijrah. When the Prophet emigrated to Madinah, they remained behind and did not emigrate. When the day of Badr came, the disbelievers took them along with their own people to Badr against their will, and they were killed among the disbelievers.

His saying ﴿wronging themselves﴾ means: by associating partners with God (shirk), for they were killed as polytheists, since acceptance of Islam after the Prophet's Hijrah was not possible except through emigration. Then this was lifted by his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "There is no hijrah after the conquest."

﴿They will say: In what [condition] were you?﴾ That is, the angels said to those who had embraced Islam but did not emigrate: ﴿In what [condition] were you?﴾ That is, in which of the two groups were you, among the Muslims or among the polytheists? This is a question of reproach, not a question seeking information. ﴿They will say: We were oppressed in the land﴾ That is, we were in Makkah, oppressed among the polytheists. ﴿They [the angels] will say﴾ That is, the angels: ﴿Was not the earth of God spacious, so that you could emigrate therein?﴾ That is, to Madinah. ﴿Their refuge is Hell, and evil is the destination﴾: He pronounced for them the Fire, because they died as polytheists.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 98:

﴿Except the oppressed among men, women and children﴾ who are those with valid excuses. Among them were al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, and Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "I and my mother were among the oppressed in Makkah, and they are those for whom the Prophet (ﷺ) supplicated in the qunut, saying: 'O Allah, deliver al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah and the oppressed in Makkah, and tighten Your grip upon Mudar.' He would supplicate for them in this manner for a month, until they were delivered and arrived [in Madinah]. Then he abandoned that supplication, and he was asked about it, and he said: 'Do you not see that they have arrived?'"

﴿They are not able to devise a plan﴾, meaning: to leave [Makkah]; ﴿nor are they guided to a way﴾, meaning: a path to Madinah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 99:

﴿Then those — it is hoped that Allah will pardon them﴾ "Asa" (it is hoped) from Allah is obligatory, because it is for raising hope (al-it'ma'), and Allah, exalted is He, when He raises a servant's hope, makes it incumbent upon Himself and brings him to it.

﴿And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ It is related that when this verse was revealed, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah wrote it to the oppressed (al-mustad'afin) in Makkah. Among them was an elderly man called Jundu' ibn Damrah, and it is said he was called Habib ibn Damrah. He said: "I am not among the oppressed, and I know the way to Madinah." He said to his sons: "Carry me to Madinah." So they carried him, bringing him along, and when he reached al-Tan'im, death overtook him. When this reached the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, they said: "Had he reached Madinah, Allah would have completed his reward." So there was revealed the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah﴾. Meaning: his reward was completed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 100:

And His saying: ﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on the earth many a refuge and abundance﴾. Al-muraghim (the one who seeks refuge): the muhājir (emigrant), and al-muraghama (the act of turning away from one's people): al-muhājara (emigration), the muhājir. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: Emigration was only called muraghama because whoever emigrates leaves (yurāghim) his people and his kin. And the poet said:

(Like a mountain that takes refuge in its own sides, / mighty in its refuge and its place of escape.)

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "muraghaman" means a place of transfer to which one moves. Mujāhid said: "muraghaman" means one who moves away and removes himself. And His saying: ﴿wasʿah﴾ (abundance). Ibn ʿAbbās said: its meaning is abundance in provision. Qatādah said: its meaning is abundance from misguidance to guidance.

﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah﴾. We have already mentioned in what matter it was revealed. ﴿And Allah is ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 101:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And when you travel through the land﴾, meaning: when you journey, ﴿there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve will afflict you﴾.

There is no disagreement that shortening the prayer during travel is permissible in a state of fear. As for a state of security: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said that it is not permissible. This was also the view of Dawud (al-Zahiri) and the People of the Literal Reading (Ahl al-Zahir), who adhered to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. But the majority of scholars, and this is the view of most of the Ummah, said that shortening is permissible in a state of security, based on what is related from Ya'la ibn Umayya, who said to Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "What is the matter with us that we shorten, when we are secure, and Allah the Exalted says in His Book: ﴿that you shorten the prayer if you fear﴾?" Umar said: "I wondered at what you wondered at, so I asked the Prophet, and he said: 'It is a charity which Allah has given you, so accept His charity.'" And it is related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) travelled from Makkah to Madinah, fearing none but Allah, and shortened the prayer. He (ﷺ) used to shorten the prayer on all his journeys, and it is not reported that he ever completed it on any journey. For this reason al-Shafi'i said: shortening is preferable, though completing is also permissible.

It is related from Jabir and al-Hasan, and this is the view of Ibn Abbas, that the prayer of residence is four rak'ahs, the prayer of travel is two rak'ahs, and the prayer of fear is one rak'ah. It is also related from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Allah the Exalted ordained the prayer through the tongue of His Prophet: in residence four rak'ahs, in travel two rak'ahs, and in fear one rak'ah." Most of the Ummah hold that shortening in fear is two rak'ahs, like the shortening of travel. Then they differed about shortening into two opinions: whether it is a permission (ibahah) or an obligation (wajib). Some said it is a permission, and this is the choice of al-Shafi'i, and it is the more correct view, because of the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, and this is like His words: ﴿there is no blame upon them both if they return to one another﴾.

Others said it is obligatory. The difference among the early scholars on this is well known.

As for His words: ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will afflict you﴾, meaning: they will kill you, and the word "fitnah" here carries the meaning of killing. Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited: "that you shorten the prayer, that those who disbelieve will afflict you," omitting the words ﴿if you fear﴾. It is related from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari that he said: the words ﴿there is no blame upon you that you shorten the prayer﴾ were revealed in this amount only, then a year passed and nothing was revealed; so the Messenger of Allah was asked about the prayer of fear, and then there was revealed: (﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will afflict you; indeed the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy﴾, and when you are among them and establish the prayer for them). So he indicated that it refers to the prayer of fear, not to the prayer of travel.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 102:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you are among them and establish prayer for them﴾, this verse explains the manner of the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf). Know that the prayer of fear is permissible after the Messenger of Allah according to the view of most scholars. Some of them said: the prayer of fear is not permissible for anyone after him, and this is the view of Abu Yusuf, holding to the apparent meaning of the verse. His saying: ﴿And when you are among them﴾ makes his presence among them a condition. The more correct view is the first. As for His saying: ﴿And when you are among them﴾, it is not in the form of a condition; rather the speech came in accordance with the circumstance. It has been reported that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah performed the prayer of fear after him.

(﴿Let them be behind you, and let another group who have not prayed come forward and pray with you, and let them take their precaution and their weapons. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your belongings so that they could turn upon you in a single assault. And there is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons because of rain or if you are ill﴾: so let one group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons.) The occasion of revelation of the verse is what Abu 'Ayyash al-Zuraqi reported: that the Messenger of Allah halted at 'Usfan, and over the cavalry of the polytheists was Khalid ibn al-Walid. The Prophet prayed with his Companions the midday prayer (salat al-zuhr). The polytheists said: "We have found them unguarded; if we attack them and charge at them..." Some of them said: "A prayer is going to come to them that is dearer to them than their children and their families," meaning the afternoon prayer (salat al-'asr). Then Gabriel descended and informed him of their statement, and he commanded the prayer of fear.

The Messenger of Allah has been reported to have performed the prayer of fear in various narrations. Al-Shafi'i adopted the narration of Salih ibn Khawwat ibn Jubayr from his father from the Prophet: that he performed the prayer of fear, dividing his Companions into two groups. He led one of the two groups in one rak'ah, and they stood up and completed two rak'ahs and went toward the enemy. The second group came while the Prophet was waiting for them, and he led them in the second rak'ah and waited for them sitting until they stood and completed two rak'ahs, then he concluded the prayer with them. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So let one group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons﴾.

They differed as to when they should take up their weapons. Some said: they take them during the prayer, so that they appear more fearsome in the eyes of the enemy; accordingly they take from the weapons only what does not prevent them from performing the pillars of the prayer. Others said: they take up their weapons when they go toward the enemy.

﴿And when they have prostrated﴾, meaning: when they have prayed, ﴿let them be behind you, and let another group who have not prayed come forward and pray with you, and let them take their precaution and their weapons.﴾ Al-hadhar (precaution) is that by which one guards against the enemy. ﴿Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect﴾, meaning: if they found you heedless, ﴿your weapons and your belongings﴾, meaning: during the prayer, ﴿so they could turn upon you in a single assault﴾, meaning: they would charge at you in one charge.

﴿And there is no blame upon you if there is discomfort from rain or if you are ill that you put down your weapons﴾. He granted them leniency in putting down the weapons in the case of rain and illness, because the weapon is heavy to carry in these two conditions. ﴿And take your precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 103:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when you have completed the prayer﴾, meaning: the prayer of fear (ṣalāt al-khawf). ﴿Remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾, meaning: remembrance through glorification (tasbīḥ), declaring His oneness (tahlīl), praising Him (taḥmīd), and extolling Him (tamjīd). ﴿And when you are secure﴾, meaning: when you have settled, resided, and become safe. ﴿Then establish the prayer﴾, meaning: perform it in its pillars (arkān) and its form, as you have known it. ﴿Indeed, the prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾. Mujahid said: that is, an obligation fixed (muwaqqatan) to be performed at its appointed times. Zayd ibn Aslam said: He meant by it an obligation issued in installments (manjaman), coming one portion after another.

**The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 4, verse 104:**

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not falter in pursuing the people. If you are suffering pain, then indeed they suffer pain just as you suffer pain﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse: "On the day of Uhud, when the disbelievers were defeated, the Prophet (ﷺ) sent a group of his Companions after them. They complained of the pain of their wounds, so the verse was revealed: ﴿And do not falter in pursuing the people﴾," meaning: do not weaken in seeking the people. ﴿If you are suffering pain﴾, meaning: you are in agony and complain of pain. ﴿Then indeed they suffer pain﴾, meaning: they are in agony and complain of pain, ﴿just as you suffer pain﴾. The poet said on this meaning:

(Fight the people, O Khuza'a, and let them not deter you
from fighting them. The people are like you in their wounds,
hair on the head that does not spread out when they are killed.)

﴿And you hope from God what they do not hope﴾, meaning: you hope from God what they do not hope for, namely victory in this world and reward in the Hereafter. Al-Farra' and al-Kisa'i said: "Hope (raja') here means fear (khawf), and every one who hopes is also fearful, because he fears that he will not attain what he hopes for." From this is His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not look to God with reverence?﴾ They all agreed that its meaning is: "What is the matter with you that you do not fear God's greatness?" The poet said:

(You do not hope when the two [armies] meet, [whether you face] seven [enemies] together or one alone.)

﴿And God is ever Knowing, Wise﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 105:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse: it is related that Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, from the clan of Zafar ibn al-Harith, stole a coat of mail. When he brought it to them, he threw it into the house of a Jew, and said: "He stole it." And in another narration: he deposited it with a Jew. When it was discovered, he said: "The Jew stole it." So his people, who were the Banu Zafar ibn al-Harith, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) to defend him, and they wanted the Prophet (ﷺ) to ward off the theft from him and to cut off the hand of the Jew, while it was known among his people that he was the thief. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾, meaning: so that you may judge with truth. ﴿That you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, meaning: by what He has taught you. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Beware of personal opinion (ra'y), for the Exalted says: ﴿by what Allah has shown you﴾, and He did not say: 'by what you think.'" ﴿And do not be a pleader for the treacherous﴾, meaning: Tu'mah is among the treacherous, so do not be a defender of him.
﴿And ask Allah for forgiveness﴾: He commanded him to seek forgiveness, because he had intended to defend him (the man accused of theft). ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 107:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, meaning: those who betray themselves. The ikhtiyan (betrayal) is an iftial form derived from khiyanah (betrayal, treachery). ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love﴾: the people of tafsir said its meaning is: Indeed, Allah does not draw near to ﴿one who is a betrayer, sinful﴾. Al-Khawwan is the traitor (al-kha'in), and al-Athim is one possessed of sin (dhu al-ithm).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 4, verse 108:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They hide themselves from the people, but they cannot hide themselves from Allah, and He is with them﴾, concerning the complaint of the Banu Zafar ibn al-Harith. Its meaning: they conceal themselves from the people, and do not conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them. ﴿When they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾. We have already explained that tabyit (plotting, planning) is the arranging of an action at night. That plotting on their part was that the people of Tu'mah said: "We will refer his case to the Prophet, for he will hear his oath, and his statement, because he is a Muslim, and he will not hear from the Jew, because he is a disbeliever." So Allah, may He be exalted, did not approve of their saying. ﴿And Allah is ever encompassing of what you do﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 109:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Here you are, you who⁠ argued on their behalf in the life of this world﴾. He means: "You, O these people." Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj, the grammarian) said: its meaning is: "Here you are, you who argued⁠ on their behalf in the life of this world," i.e., you disputed. The root of al-jidal (argumentation, disputation) is al-jadl, which is twisting (fatl). It is said: "a person is ajdal" when he is firmly built in creation, and the falcon is called ajdal because it is the strongest of birds in hunting.

﴿Who, then, will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾ He means: who is it that will take charge of their affairs and defend them on the Day of Resurrection?

Almost certainly not: this is a translation task, and I should produce it directly.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 110:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾. In this verse He offered repentance to Ta'mah and his people, and commanded them to seek forgiveness.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself﴾. The occasion of this (revelation) was that his people said to him: "Repent to Allah." So he swore that he had not stolen it, and that it was the Jew who had stolen it. This is what Allah the Exalted refers to in His words, "and whoever earns sin..." ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 112:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever earns a sin or a wrong﴾ is his theft which we mentioned, ﴿then throws it onto an innocent person﴾ is his attributing the theft to the Jew, who was innocent of it, ﴿then he has borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾. Al-buhtan (slander) is the lie that a person is bewildered by, and it is the bahtah (bewilderment); and by the manifest sin he meant the false oath (al-yamin al-fajirah).

"The Most High said: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ This is an address to the Messenger. ﴿A group of them had resolved to lead you astray﴾, meaning: the people of Ṭuʿmah (Ṭuʿmah's clan) intended to confuse you, so that you would defend him. ﴿But they lead astray none except themselves﴾, meaning: its harm returns upon them. ﴿And they do not harm you at all﴾, meaning: its harm returns upon them and does not harm you, because you are protected (maʿṣūm). ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾. It was said: He meant by this, "And Allah has sent down to you the Book with wisdom." And it was said: by "the Book" is meant the Qur'an, and by "wisdom" the Sunnah. ﴿And taught you what you did not know﴾, meaning: of the rulings of the Qur'an. And it was said: of the knowledge of the unseen. And it was said: He taught you your worth, which you did not know. ﴿And the grace of Allah upon you has been ever great﴾."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 114:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity﴾. Al-najwa (secret counsel): the private matters of planning. Al-Zajjaj said: whatever a group keeps to itself and deliberates over is najwa, whether secret or public, and here He intends the secret talk of the people of Ṭu'ma and their scheming. It was also said that it applies to all events.

﴿Except for one who enjoins charity﴾. It was said: He means, except the secret talk of one who enjoins charity. It was also said: this is an exception of a disconnected type (istithna' munqati'), meaning: but rather, one who enjoins charity ﴿or what is right (ma'ruf)﴾, which is everything the Law recognizes, ﴿or reconciliation between people﴾. And in a report: "All of the son of Adam's speech is against him, except three: enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, or the remembrance of God." When Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated this hadith, it was said to him: "How severe this hadith is!" He said: "Recite His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity﴾, and so on."

It is also narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari: "Shall I direct you to a charity that is better for you than red camels?" – i.e., than charity given in red camels? – He said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." He said: "That you reconcile between people when they fall into discord, and that you bring them close when they have drifted apart."

﴿And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of God, We shall give him a great reward﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 115:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾. He meant by this Ṭu'mah, who argued with the Prophet, then joined (the polytheists) in Mecca, and apostatized when the ruling of amputation (for theft) was enforced upon him.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When he joined (the polytheists) in Mecca, he stole there, and was found breaking into a house to steal, and he was killed.

In some narratives: When he joined (the polytheists) in Mecca, he stayed with al-Hajjaj ibn Ghallat al-Aslami. He got up during part of the night to steal, and they sensed him, seized him and gathered around him. They said: "He is a guest," and let him go. So he joined the tribe of Banu Sulaym, who worshipped idols, and died upon that. Concerning him the verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾, because when he apostatized, he followed other than the way of the believers.

The scholars of the religion used this verse as evidence that consensus (ijma') is a proof (ḥujjah).

His saying: ﴿We shall leave him to what he has turned to﴾, i.e., We shall leave him to what he himself chose. It was also said: We shall leave him to whoever he has taken as an ally. ﴿And We shall burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 116:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.﴾ We have already mentioned the meaning of this verse earlier. ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray.﴾ Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi related with his chain of narration from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "This is the verse most beloved to me in the Qur'an."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 117:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They invoke, apart from Him, none but females﴾, meaning: they invoke, apart from Him, none but ﴿females﴾. It has been said: its meaning is the idols. The idols were called "females" only because they used to give them female names, saying: al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat. They also used to say of the idol of each tribe: "the female of the sons of so-and-so." Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "With every idol there was a jinn-female from among the devils." It has also been said: its meaning is the lifeless things. Lifeless things were called "females" because females are the lowest and most inferior of the two sexes, and likewise lifeless things are more base than living beings; their idols were made of lifeless matter and inanimate stone.

Al-Dahhak said: he meant by it the angels, for they used to say: "The angels are females." Some of them worshipped the angels and fashioned idols in the forms of angels. Ibn 'Abbas recited ﴿ināthan﴾ as "unthan," the plural of al-awthan (idols), and it is also recorded as an irregular (shadhdh) reading "inathan," the plural of al-inath (females), so it would be a plural of plural, like "mithl" and "amthal." ﴿And they invoke none but a rebellious devil﴾, because when they worship idols, they have obeyed Satan. By it he meant Iblis. The word murid means the obstinate, the rebellious, and its root meaning is one stripped of all good; from it comes "al-amrad" (the beardless), and it is said: "a shajara mirda'" (a tree whose branches have fallen off) when its branches have shed.

**[Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 118]**

﴿Allah has cursed him﴾. That is, Allah has removed him far from mercy as a punishment. For this reason it is not permissible to curse animals, since they do not deserve punishment or expulsion from mercy.

﴿And he said, "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion"﴾. That is, a known measure. It has been said in the exegesis: from every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine go to Satan and one goes to Allah.

The root meaning of al-fard (فَرْض, "appointed, obligatory") is cutting and notching. From it comes fard al-qaws (فَرْض القوس), which is the slit in which the bowstring is placed. From it also comes fard al-siwak (فَرْض السِّواك), which is the place where the thread is fixed to it. From it also comes fardat al-bahr (فَرْضة البحر), which is the landing place where the ship is brought to a halt. Al-farḍ (الفَرْض) is also a type of date that grows in Oman. The poet said:

*"When I eat fish and fardh dates, / I go long and I go wide."*

"The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And I will mislead them﴾, meaning: I will lead them astray. If someone says: how is misleading attributed to Him, when it is not His to cause misguidance? We say: its meaning is adornment (tazyin) and calling to misguidance. Indeed He said: "I was sent as a caller, and nothing of guidance is in my hands; and Satan was sent as one who adorns, and nothing of misguidance is in his hands." ﴿And I will arouse false desires in them﴾. It was said: its meaning is: I will make them desire the pursuit of their whims. And it was said: its meaning is: I will make them desire long life in bliss, so that they prefer this world over the Hereafter. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: I will make them desire attaining the Hereafter while persisting in sins.

﴿And I will command them, and they will slit the ears of the cattle﴾. He meant by this the bahira, which is mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah. Al-batk means cutting, and what is meant by it is splitting the ears. ﴿And I will command them, and they will alter the creation of Allah﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, in one of the two narrations, and it is the statement of Mujahid, said: its meaning is: they will alter the religion of Allah, that is, placing in the religion: making lawful what is unlawful, forbidding what is lawful, and the like. The second narration from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the statement of Anas and 'Ikrimah, is that it means: castrating animals. Anas used to dislike castrating beasts for this reason, while al-Hasan permitted it. Ibn Mas'ud said: it means tattooing. It may also be that what is meant is changing lineages, that is, a person transferring from one lineage to another. It may also be that what is meant is dyeing with black, which is forbidden; the permitted dye is only with red or yellow. ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah﴾, that is, follows him by obeying him, ﴿has certainly suffered a manifest loss﴾."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 120:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He promises them﴾. His promising may be by way of frightening, as God the Exalted said: ﴿The Devil promises you poverty﴾. It was also said that he takes on the form of a human being, and so promises and holds out hopes. He appeared on the day of Badr in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum, and he appeared on the day when the Quraysh gathered and consulted about expelling the Prophet, in the form of an old man from Najd.

His saying ﴿and arouses their desires﴾ has already been mentioned. Among this is a person's wishing (tamanni) to fulfil his appetites.

Know that a person is not held to account for being overcome by desire or for craving appetites, because that is something he was created with. He is held to account for wishing (tamanni), such as wishing for wine in order to drink it, or for a woman in order to commit adultery with her. That is from disobedience, and he is held to account for it. ﴿And the Devil promises them nothing but delusion﴾. Delusion (al-ghurur) is the imagining of reaching a benefit from a place of harm.
﴿Those, their refuge is Hell, and they will not find any escape from it.﴾ Meaning: no place of turning away (معدلا, ma'adilan).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 122:

The Exalted One said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true.﴾ If it is said: What is the benefit in repeating the promise and the threat in the Qur'an? It is said: its benefit is emphasis, to make it definite beyond any possibility of interpretation (ta'wil). It was also said: the promise is repeated concerning the details of faith, and the threat is repeated concerning the details of disbelief. ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾ That is: in speech.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 123:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾. Masruq said, he is Abu 'Aisha Masruq ibn al-Ajda' al-Hamdani: He meant by it: "It is not by your wishful thinking, O Muslims, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book, who are the Jews and the Christians."

Mujahid said: By His saying ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking﴾ He meant the idolaters of the Arabs, and ﴿nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾, meaning: the Jews and the Christians. According to the first view, the meaning of the verse is that the Jews said: "We have the better claim, because our religion is older and our scripture is older."

And the Christians said: "We have the better claim, because we follow the religion of Jesus, who is the Spirit of God and His Word, and who used to give life to the dead."

And the Muslims said: "We have the better claim, because our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our scripture abrogates the (previous) scriptures, and we have believed in your scripture, while you have not believed in our scripture." God, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾, meaning: the matter is not by wishful thinking, but the matter is by righteous deeds. He has said: "Religion is not by wishful thinking, nor by adornment..." the report.

As for the second view, the meaning of the verse is that the Jews and the Christians said: "We are the people of Paradise," and this is the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿And they say: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾. The idolaters said: "There is no Paradise, no Fire, and no resurrection." God, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾, i.e.: it is not as the idolaters said, nor as the Jews and the Christians said.

﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and a group of the exegetes said: the verse is general in application to every doer (of evil). Al-Hasan said: by it He meant the people of polytheism.

In the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "When this verse was revealed, the Companions said: 'Which of us has not done evil?' The verse weighed heavily upon them, so they returned to the Messenger of God concerning this, and he said: 'There is not one of you to whom a calamity befalls except that it expiates for him, even the thorn that pricks him and the setback that afflicts him.'"

It is also related: "Abu Bakr entered upon the Messenger of God, and the Messenger of God said to him: 'Shall I recite to you a verse that was revealed to me?' He said: 'Yes.' So he recited: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾. Abu Bakr said: 'I felt a breaking in my back,' so he (peace be upon him) said: 'What is the matter with you, Abu Bakr?' I said: 'How is there salvation after this verse? We are destroyed! Which of us has not done evil?' He said: 'As for you, Abu Bakr, and the believers, you are recompensed for it in this world, so you meet God, exalted is He, with no sin upon you. As for the disbelievers, it is gathered for them, and then they are recompensed for it in the Hereafter.'" In another narration, he (peace be upon him) said to him: "Do you not become weary? Do you not grieve? Do you not fall ill? Does not hardship befall you? That is what you are recompensed for." This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself, besides God, any protector or helper﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 124:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and they will not be wronged the least bit (naqir).﴾ That is: the measure of a naqir (a small dent in a date-pit). This is because, when God, may He be exalted, left creation to be judged by their deeds, He made clear in these verses the relation between the deed and its recompense.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 125:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself entirely to Allah﴾, meaning: he who sincerely devotes his worship to Allah. It was also said: he who directs his worship to Allah. The word "wajh" (face) is used with the meaning of religion and worship, and from this is the saying of the one who prays: "I have turned my face," meaning: my religion, which is the prayer.

﴿While he is a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth⁠﴾. He specified Abraham because he was the most accepted by all nations. It was also said: because he [the Prophet] was sent upon the religion of Abraham, and some things were added to it for him.

﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend⁠﴾, meaning: a beloved, with no deficiency in his love. Al-khullah (intimate friendship) is the purity of affection, so its meaning is that He took him as a beloved, made him His chosen one, and made him exclusively His own, as a beloved is with a beloved. The poet said:

(He has penetrated the passage of my spirit, / and thus was the Khalil (intimate friend) named Khalil)

It was also said: the one in need, from al-khullah, which is need (al-hajah), meaning: He made his need directed to Himself alone, not to others. The poet said:

(If a friend comes to him on a day of request, / he says: "My wealth is not absent, nor is my sanctuary forbidden," meaning: if a needy person comes to him.)

The first interpretation is more sound, because His saying ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend⁠﴾ requires intimacy from both sides, and need cannot be conceived from both sides. In a report he said: "Allah has taken me as an intimate friend just as He took Abraham as an intimate friend. Had I been taking an intimate friend, I would have taken Abu Bakr; but it is affection and brotherhood of faith. Indeed, your companion is the intimate friend of Allah."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah has been ever, of all things, All-Encompassing.﴾ Al-Muhit (the All-Encompassing) is the one who knows a thing in all the aspects in which knowledge of it can be conceived.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 127:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women﴾, meaning: they seek your ruling concerning women. It has been said: this refers to Umm Kajjah, and we have already explained her story, and that the people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) did not give inheritance to women and children.

﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, He gives you a ruling as it is recited to you in the Book, ﴿concerning the orphan women﴾. This is the attribution of a thing to itself, because by "orphans" he meant the women, ﴿to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them﴾. Al-Hasan and a group said: he meant by this, you do not give them their rights of inheritance. ﴿And you desire to marry them﴾ (lit. "and you desire to marry them" with the preposition "bi" in the sense of "an", that is: from marrying them) because of their unattractiveness, and they applied the verse to inheritance.

ʿĀʾishah said: he meant by this, you do not give them what has been prescribed for them of the dowry (ṣadāq, the bridal gift). His saying ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾ means: in marrying them. ﴿And the weak among the children﴾ means: and He gives you a ruling concerning the weak among the children, namely the young ones. ﴿And that you should stand up for the orphans with justice﴾, that is, with equity. ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 128:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment (nushuz) or aversion﴾. Nushuz (rebellion/ill-treatment) is elevation; what is meant by it is the husband's elevating himself and being arrogant toward his wife. His saying: ﴿that they make a settlement between themselves, a settlement﴾ means: that she gives up some of her turn, and agrees that the turn be greater for the young woman. It was also said: it is a settlement concerning the dower by remitting it, and the like. The second opinion: the verse was revealed concerning Sawdah bint Zam'ah. ﴿And settlement is better﴾. It was said: he meant by it that settlement is better than separation. Al-Sam'ani's commentary (Tafsir al-Quran) on Surah 4, verse 131:

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and [you], [to], "Fear Allah."﴾ This is Allah's commandment to His servants to have taqwa (God-consciousness, piety).

( ﴿And if you disbelieve, then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy.﴾

To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is sufficient as Guardian (wakil). If it is asked: what is the benefit in repeating His saying, ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾? It is answered: each of the two occurrences has its own meaning.

As for the first: its meaning is, "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He enjoins upon you taqwa (God-consciousness), so fear Him and accept His command."

As for the second: it says, "Indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever Rich, Praiseworthy; so ask from Him what you seek."

As for the third: it says, "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is sufficient as Guardian," meaning: take Him as your guardian and do not rely upon anyone else.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 133:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others﴾. It is related: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to strike the shoulder of Salman with his hand, and recite: ﴿and bring others﴾, and say: 'Salman and his companions.'" ﴿And Allah is ever Competent to do that.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 134:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾. He meant by this: the disbelievers, for they act seeking the reward of this world and desiring its bliss, and they do not seek the reward of the Hereafter, nor do they believe in it. So Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter, and Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 135:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistent in upholding justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more capable of looking after them both. So do not follow [your] desire, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse to give it, then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.﴾

Al-qawwam: an intensive form of al-qa'im (the one who stands firm). Al-qist: justice (al-'adl). Its meaning: be those who speak with justice. ﴿Witnesses for Allah﴾: because when they bear witness to the truth and stand firmly by justice, they are witnesses for Allah. ﴿Even if it be against yourselves﴾: If it is said, "How can one bear witness against himself?" It is said: his testimony against himself is acknowledgment (al-iqrar), and this is the meaning of what is related from Ibn 'Abbas: "Speak the truth, even if it be against yourselves."

﴿Or parents and relatives﴾: that is, speak the truth even if it be against parents and relatives. It is said: the verse was revealed concerning a man who held testimony against his father, and he intended to refrain from giving it; then the words ﴿or parents and relatives﴾ were revealed.

﴿Whether one is rich or poor﴾: al-Suddi said: this was revealed concerning two men who brought a dispute before the Prophet (ﷺ), one of whom was rich and the other poor. The Prophet (ﷺ) inclined toward the poor man, because he judged that the poor man would not dispute falsely, while the right lay with the rich man in reality. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿whether one is rich or poor﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is: do not argue against the rich man because of his wealth, nor show mercy to the poor man because of his poverty. 'Ata' said: do not be unjust toward the poor man, and do not glorify the rich man. This is the meaning of the verse. The essential meaning is: stand firm in testimony, whether the one testified against is rich or poor, and whether the one in whose favour it is given is rich or poor; do not refrain from testifying for the rich because of his wealth, nor from testifying against the poor because of his poverty.

His saying: ﴿whether one is rich or poor﴾: that is, whether the one testified against is rich or poor. ﴿Allah is more capable of looking after them both﴾: that is, entrust their affair to Allah. al-Hasan said: its meaning is: Allah knows them both better. ﴿So do not follow [your] desire, lest you not be just﴾: it is said: its meaning is: do not follow desire by being unjust, that is, so that you may be just, as one says, "Do not disobey, so that your Lord will be pleased." It is also said: its meaning is: do not follow desire so as to deviate from truth to falsehood. ﴿And if you distort﴾: it derives from al-layy (distortion). The poet said:

(I had dealt with him kindly... for fear of bankruptcy and procrastination)

As to its meaning there are two views. First: it is addressed to the rulers, and the meaning of ﴿if you distort﴾ is that you incline toward one of the two disputants, or turn away from him.

Second, which is the view of most exegetes: it is addressed to the witnesses. Distortion among them is altering the testimony, and turning away is concealing the testimony. The first is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

As for the second reading, "wa in talu" (and if you neglect): there are two views concerning it. First: its original form is "wa in talwu," and one of the two waws was merged into the other for lightness; the meaning is as we have explained. Second: it is from al-wilaya, meaning: if you neglect the upholding of the duty of testimony, ﴿or refuse﴾, so that you abandon discharging the testimony. ﴿Then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 136:

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾. Most of the exegetes (mufassirun) hold that it refers to the believers, and its meaning is: O you who have believed, remain steadfast in belief (iman), as one says to a man who is standing, "Stand until I return to you," meaning: remain standing.

Mujahid said: it is an address to the hypocrites (munafiqun), and its meaning is: O you who have believed with the tongue, believe with the heart. Al-Dahhak, and it is also a narration of al-Kalbi from Ibn 'Abbas, said: it is an address to the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab), and its meaning is: O you who have believed in Musa and 'Isa, believe in Muhammad. ﴿And the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿and the Book which He sent down before﴾, meaning: the books sent down before the Qur'an.

﴿And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray﴾, meaning: far from the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 137:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief﴾. Qatadah said: This refers to the Jews. They believed in Musa, then disbelieved in him by worshipping the calf, then believed in Musa through repentance, then disbelieved in Isa, then increased in disbelief by disbelieving in Muhammad. It was also said: It refers to all the People of the Book, both Jews and Christians: they believed in their prophet, then disbelieved in him, and believed in their scripture, then disbelieved in it, then increased in disbelief by disbelieving in Muhammad. Mujahid said: It refers to a people who apostatised: they believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised.

And regarding the like of this, is their repentance accepted?

Ali said: Their repentance is not accepted, for when one believes, then disbelieves, then believes, then disbelieves, then if he wishes to believe, it is not accepted from him, and he is put to death. This is based on the words of the Exalted: ﴿Allah would not forgive them﴾.

But most of the scholars hold that their repentance is accepted. It is possible that the verse refers to the hypocrites and a group of the People of the Book, who professed belief with their tongues, then returned to disbelief, then came back, believed, then returned to disbelief again.

﴿Allah would not forgive them﴾. If it is asked: What is the meaning of the words of the Exalted: ﴿Allah would not forgive them﴾, when it is known that Allah does not forgive disbelief? It is answered: Al-Naqqash (al-Naqqash) explained in his tafsir that its meaning is: when a disbeliever embraces Islam, his former disbelief is forgiven him. So this one who embraced Islam, then disbelieved, then embraced Islam, then disbelieved, his former disbelief, which would have been forgiven had he remained upon Islam, is not forgiven. ﴿Nor will He guide them to a way﴾, that is, a path to the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 138:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Give the hypocrites the good news that there is a painful punishment for them.﴾ If it is asked: What is the meaning of giving good news of a painful punishment? It is said: The original sense of bushra (glad tidings) is every report by which the complexion of the face changes, whether pleasant or unpleasant. However, it is in most cases used only for a pleasant report. So when it is used for an unpleasant report, it is in keeping with the original sense. It is also said: He meant by it: place this in the position of glad tidings, just as the Arabs say: "Your greeting is the whip, and your punishment is the sword."

That is, you placed the whip in the position of the greeting. The poet said:

(And horses that have advanced upon horses... their greeting among them is a painful striking.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 139:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾. This refers to the hypocrites, who used to befriend the disbelievers and thought that victory and dominance belonged to them. ﴿Do they seek honour with them?﴾ That is: do they seek strength and dominance from them? ﴿Surely honour belongs to God entirely﴾.
