If someone says: We see that in some circumstances dominance belongs to the disbelievers, so what is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Surely honour belongs to God entirely﴾? It is said: its meaning is that the One who grants strength is God, may He be exalted, in all circumstances.

It is also said: its meaning is that dominance through proof belongs to God entirely.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 140:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being rejected and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a conversation other than that; indeed, you would then be like them.﴾

This is a reference to what was revealed in Surah al-An'am: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them...﴾ [6:68], the verse. It prohibits sitting with them. And what is the ruling on sitting with them? As for one who sits with them and is pleased with what they engage in, he is a disbeliever like them, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿indeed, you would then be like them.﴾ But if he sits and is not pleased with what they engage in, then it is better that he not sit; yet if he sits while disliking it, he does not become a disbeliever. This is the ruling concerning every innovation (bid'ah) that is debated. So if they leave off discussing it and engage in a conversation other than it, there is no harm in sitting with them even though one dislikes it, because of His saying: ﴿until they engage in a conversation other than that.﴾ Al-Hasan said: Even if they engage in a conversation other than it, it is not permissible to sit with them, because of His saying in Surah al-An'am: ﴿And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.﴾ [6:68] But most scholars hold that it is permissible. The verse of al-An'am is Meccan and this verse is Medinan, and the later (revelation) takes precedence.

{Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell, all of them.

(Those who wait in suspense about you:) that is, the hypocrites who await your outcome. (If there comes to you a victory from God,) that is, a triumph. ﴿They say, "Were we not with you?"﴾ that is, "We were with you, so give us a share of the spoils." ﴿And if the disbelievers get a portion,﴾ that is, if the strength lies with the disbelievers, ﴿they say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?"﴾ (Istihwadh) means taking control and dominance, and from it is the words of God Most High: {Satan has gained mastery over them}. Al-Mubarrad said: the meaning of this is: they say, "Did we not overpower you in your opinion, protect you from the believers, and keep you from entering their ranks, and discourage the believers from you?"

Another commentator said: its meaning is: "Did we not take control over you by supporting you, through our informing you of the news and affairs of the believers, and by our discouraging them from you?" ﴿So God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers.﴾ Ali and Ibn Abbas said: He meant by this: on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: it is the way of proof, meaning: the disbelievers will never have a proof over the believers, ever.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 142:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them﴾. "They deceive Allah" means: they treat Allah in the manner of those who deceive, in that they show faith and conceal disbelief. "And He is deceiving them" means: He treats them in the manner of those who deceive. This is in two respects. The first: He judges them to be believers outwardly and disbelievers inwardly, just as they did. The second: on the Day of Resurrection, He gives them light, as He gives the believers light; then, when they are on the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), their light is extinguished, and the believers depart with their light. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and He is deceiving them﴾. It was also said: its meaning is: they deceive the Messenger of Allah, and He is deceiving them, that is, He requites them for their deceiving of the Messenger. The second was called deception by way of pairing, as He said: ﴿and the recompense for an evil deed is an evil deed like it﴾.

In the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Some people will be brought on the Day of Resurrection to Paradise, until, when they approach it and smell its fragrance and see the bliss in it, Allah, may He be exalted, commands that they be turned away from it. They will return with a regret such that the first and the last have not returned with the like of it. They will say: 'O Lord, if You had admitted us into the Fire before You showed us what You have shown us, it would have been easier for us.' Allah, may He be exalted, will say: 'That is what I intended for you. When you were alone, you defied Me with great sins; and when you met people, you met them humbly. You feared people and did not fear Me; you honoured people and did not honour Me; you abandoned [acts] for people and did not abandon [them] for Me. So today I will make you taste the punishment, along with what you have been deprived of of the reward.'"

His saying: ﴿And when they stand up to the prayer, they stand up lazily﴾ means: sluggishly. This is the habit of the hypocrites, due to the scarcity of their motives. As for the believers, they rise eagerly to prayer, due to the abundance of their motives. ﴿They show off to people﴾ means: they do what they do to be seen by people, not in obedience to the command of Allah.

Know that showing off (riya') does not entail disbelief; it is a great fault. As for hypocrisy (nifaq), it is pure disbelief.

﴿And they remember Allah only a little﴾. Al-Hasan said: because when their deeds were not accepted, [the remembrance] was little.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 143:

﴿Wavering between that⁠﴾ means: wavering (mutadhabdhabin). Thus Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited it, and its meaning is: vacillating and bewildered. ﴿Neither to these nor to those⁠﴾, meaning: neither to the disbelievers, by openly declaring polytheism, nor to the believers, by holding the belief of faith.

Ibn 'Umar narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The likeness of the hypocrite is like the restless sheep between two flocks: if it goes to this one, it butts it, and if it goes to that one, it butts it." ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, you will never find for him a way⁠﴾, meaning: whoever Allah leaves astray, you will never find for him a path to the truth.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾. In the verse, He forbids allying with the disbelievers in preference to the believers. ﴿Do you wish to give Allah against yourselves a clear authority?﴾ As-sultan (authority): it means the proof. From this root it is said of a ruler that he is a sultan, because he holds proof. Its meaning: Do you wish to give Allah a clear proof against you in your punishment, such that you have no excuse left before Him?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 145:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾. It is also read "fi al-darak" with the letter rā' vowelless (fi al-darkˤ, with sukūn). Abū ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash said: the Fire has levels (darakāt), and Paradise has ranks (darajāt). The scholars said: it is possible that Pharaoh and Hāmān will be punished more severely than the hypocrites, even though the hypocrites are in the lowest depth. Ibn Masʿūd said: "The lowest depth is a coffin of iron, locked over them." It was also said: "It is a coffin of fire." Abū Hurayra said: "The lowest depth is a closed house upon them, in which the fire blazes above them and beneath them." ﴿And you will not find for them any helper﴾, meaning any protector from the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 146:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except for those who repent﴾, meaning: they embrace Islam. ﴿And amend﴾, meaning: they persist in repentance. ﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾. I'tisam (holding fast) is abstaining from something one fears by means of something else; so holding fast to Allah is abstaining, through obedience to Him, from everything one fears, both in this world and in the next. ﴿And are sincere in their religion for Allah﴾. Sincerity is a condition of the heart, because the verse concerns the hypocrites, and hypocrisy is disbelief of the heart; its removal is achieved through sincerity. ﴿Then those will be with the believers. And Allah will give the believers a great reward﴾. And the reason He did not say, "Then they are the believers, and Allah will give them a great reward," is out of anger toward the hypocrites.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 147:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?﴾ This is an interrogative used in the sense of affirmation (taqrir), and its meaning is: Allah does not punish the believing grateful one. The implied sense of His saying ﴿if you are grateful and believe﴾ is: if you believe and are grateful. Gratitude (shukr) is the opposite of disbelief (kufr). Disbelief is concealing a blessing, and gratitude is manifesting a blessing. ﴿And Allah is ever Grateful and All-Knowing﴾. Gratitude from Allah is the acceptance of the deed (qubul al-'amal), and its meaning is: Allah is ever accepting of acts of obedience (qabil lil-ta'at), All-Knowing of intentions (alim bil-niyyat).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 148:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil in speech, except by one who has been wronged.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is, "except by one who has been wronged." So it is permissible for him to mention evil openly by reporting the wrongdoing of the wrongdoer, and by invoking (du'a') against him. Al-Hasan said: his invocation against him is that he says, "O Allah, help me against him; O Allah, extract my right from him."

It was also said: it is permissible for him to revile, but only with the like of what was said to him, without exceeding it, and in a way that is not slander (qadhf). It has been related in a hadith: "The two revilers are on the one who begins, as long as the one who was wronged does not transgress." Mujahid said: this concerns a guest who comes to a people, and they do not host him or treat him well; it is permissible for him to mention their evil openly.

It is also read: "illa man zulima" with a fatha on the ẓa' and the lam.

Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is, "except one who has been wronged, so his speech of evil is excused." It was also said: this refers back to the preceding verse, and its implied sense is: "Allah does not do anything with your punishment if you are grateful and believe, except one who has done wrong." It was also said: this is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), meaning: Allah does not like the public mention of evil in speech, but He does not forbid the public mention of evil by one who has been wronged. ﴿And Allah is ever Hearing, Knowing.﴾ Hearing of your statements, Knowing of your intentions.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 149:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you disclose a good deed or conceal it﴾. Its meaning: if you disclose some of the charities, so that others may follow your example, or if you conceal it, out of fear of showing off (riya' ). ﴿Or pardon an evil﴾ that you have been afflicted with. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﹀.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 150:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers﴾. He meant by this the Jews, for when they disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ), it was as if they had disbelieved in Allah. ﴿And they intend to differentiate between Allah and His messengers﴾: they wish to believe in Allah and disbelieve in the Messenger. ﴿And they say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others"﴾: they believe in Musa (Moses), and disbelieve in ʿIsa (Jesus) and Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And they intend to adopt between that a way﴾: i.e., a doctrine (madhhab) they follow.

﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾. He affirmed their disbelief emphatically, so that it would be known that they are disbelievers absolutely, lest someone suppose that, since they believed in Allah and some of the messengers, their disbelief would not be absolute. ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾.

The Exalted said: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not make distinction between any of them—those, He will give them their rewards (ujur)﴾. He called it "reward" (ajr) figuratively, because He mentioned it in correspondence with the deed, since the deed necessitates it. This is similar to His saying, in the story of Musa: ﴿Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you for what you gave to water for us﴾. He called it "reward" in exchange for the deed, because Musa worked so that he would be rewarded for it. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 4, verse 153:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven.﴾ They are the Jews. They said to the Prophet: "We will not believe in you until you bring down to us a Book from heaven all at once, just as the Torah was sent down to Moses all at once."

Al-Hasan said: This was not a request of submission but a request of challenge and dictation. Had the Book been sent down to them all at once, as they asked, they would not have believed. God, exalted is He, does not send down signs according to the proposals of His servants; He sends them down according to His will. ﴿They asked Moses for something greater than that.﴾ That is: greater than that. ﴿So they said: Show us God plainly.﴾ That is: openly, with the eyes. This is because the Arabs used to count knowledge by the heart as sight; so He said ﴿plainly﴾ to make clear that He meant seeing with the eyes. Abu 'Ubayda said: its meaning is: they said, "Plainly: show us God." ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing.﴾ ﴿Then they took the calf﴾, meaning as a god, ﴿after the clear proofs had come to them, and We pardoned that.﴾ This contains an invitation to repentance. Its meaning is: those who committed that crime, We pardoned them; so you repent, and We will pardon you. ﴿And We gave Moses clear authority﴾, a manifest proof of miracles.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 154:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We raised above them the mountain (al-Tur) for their covenant.﴾ Al-Tur: the Mount of al-Tur. It is said: every mountain that grows something is a tur; if it does not grow anything, it is not called a tur. And al-mithaq (covenant): the pledge confirmed by an oath.

﴿And We said to them: Enter the gate prostrating.﴾ It is said: they prostrated on the sides of their faces until they entered the gate. In the narrative it is related that they said: "By this prostration the punishment has been lifted from us, so we will not abandon this prostration." And after that they used to prostrate on the sides of their faces.

﴿And We said to them: Do not transgress in the Sabbath.⁠﴾ Nafi' (according to the narration of Qalun) recited ﴿la ta'addu﴾ with the 'ayn vowelless and the dal shadda (tashdid) [i.e., تعدوا with the 'ayn sukun]. In the narration of Warsh from him, it is recited ﴿la ta'addu﴾ with the 'ayn fathah and the dal shadda. The meaning of both is: "Do not transgress in the Sabbath." ﴿And We took from them a solemn covenant.⁠﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 155:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So for their breaking their covenant﴾. Ma (ما) here is extra, serving as a connecting particle (ma li-l-silah), and it enters the speech only to magnify it and to give it emphasis. ﴿And their disbelief in the signs of God, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying "Our hearts are wrapped"﴾. We have already mentioned all of this. ﴿Rather, God has sealed upon them because of their disbelief﴾. Al-tab' (الطبع) means the seal (al-khatm). Al-Zajjaj said: He made their hearts like something sealed, which does not prosper, and never becomes sound, and into which no good enters. ﴿So they do not believe except a few﴾.

And [They were cursed] for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander. He meant by it: their attributing to Mary the act of fornication (zina).

Note on the translation: the Qur'anic quotation is rendered inside the ﴿ ﴾ markers as instructed, and the bracketed phrase "They were cursed" is not in the source text, so it should be removed if strict fidelity is required.

Corrected version, without additions:

﴿And for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander﴾. He meant by it: their attributing to Mary fornication (zina).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 157–158:

The Exalted said: ﴿And their saying, "Indeed, we killed the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them.﴾

It is said: Allah, the Exalted, cast the likeness of 'Isa upon the one who guided them to him, so they killed him. It is also said: they had imprisoned 'Isa in a house and appointed a guard over him, so Allah, the Exalted, cast the likeness of 'Isa upon the guard, and they killed him. It is also said: they did not know 'Isa by his person, but they knew him by his name, and they were seeking him. So Yahudhah (Judas), who was one of the companions of 'Isa, said to them: "Give me something and I will guide you to 'Isa." They gave him thirty dirhams, and he guided them to someone else, and they killed that other person. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿but it was made to appear so to them﴾, and ﴿Indeed, those who differ concerning it are in doubt about it﴾. That is because the man they killed, thinking him to be 'Isa, resembled him in his face but did not resemble him in his body. So disagreement arose among them: some of them said, "The one we killed was 'Isa," and some said, "It was not 'Isa." It is also said: the disagreement was between their scholars and their common folk (aghtam); for their scholars knew that they had not crucified 'Isa, while their ignorant and common folk believed that they had killed 'Isa. ﴿And they have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption﴾, meaning: no true knowledge. ﴿And they did not kill him for certain﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: His saying ﴿And they did not kill him﴾ is a complete sentence, and His saying ﴿for certain﴾ refers to what follows, and its implied meaning is: "Rather, Allah raised him to Himself." Al-Farra' said: its meaning is: "And they did not kill the one they assumed to be 'Isa with certainty that he was 'Isa." It is also said: the pronoun refers to 'Isa, meaning: "And they did not kill 'Isa for certain." ﴿Rather, Allah raised him to Himself, and Allah is ever Mighty and Wise.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 157–158:

The Exalted said: ﴿And their saying, "Indeed, we killed the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them.﴾

It is said: Allah, the Exalted, cast the likeness of 'Isa upon the one who guided them to him, so they killed him. It is also said: the pronoun refers to 'Isa, meaning: "And they did not kill 'Isa for certain." ﴿Rather, Allah raised him to Himself, and Allah is ever Mighty and Wise.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 159:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾. Its meaning: "And there is not any one of the People of the Book but that he will believe in him." It is like His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, meaning: "And there is not any one of you."

The scholars differed concerning His saying: ﴿before his death﴾. Al-Hasan (al-Basri), and this is one of the two narrations from Ibn 'Abbas, said: it is a reference to the People of the Book. He said: "None of the Jewish People of the Book exists but that he believes in 'Isa before his death, at the time of despair, when it will not benefit him." Until it was said to Ibn 'Abbas: "And if he dies by burning, or drowning, or collapse?" He said: "Yes."

Qatadah, and this is another narration from Ibn 'Abbas, said: the pronoun ("his") refers to 'Isa, meaning: "None of the People of the Book but that he believes in 'Isa before the death of 'Isa, and that is when he descends from the sky." 'Ikrimah said: this is about Muhammad (ﷺ): "None of the People of the Book but that he believes in him before death." This is a weak view, because the mention of Muhammad (ﷺ) has not occurred in the verse, while ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ refers to 'Isa.

The Exalted said: ﴿Because of the wrongdoing of those who became Jews, We forbade them good things that had been made lawful for them.﴾ It means: because of their criminal conduct that has been mentioned. "We forbade them good things that had been made lawful for them" is what we mentioned in Surah al-An'am (Chapter 6), {And to those who became Jews We forbade every animal with claws} the verse, as will come later {and their turning many away from the way of God}

Translation:

"And their taking of usury, although they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of people's wealth unjustly" (meaning: bribery). ﴿We have prepared for those among them who disbelieve a painful punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 162:

His Exalted saying: ﴿But those firmly grounded in knowledge among them﴾. "Lakin" (but) is used for turning away from one statement and entering into another. ﴿Those firmly grounded﴾ (al-rasikhun): those who go to the utmost extent in knowledge, the people of insight in it. By this he meant those scholars of the Jews who embraced Islam, such as Abdullah ibn Salam, Yamin ibn Yamin, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Ka'b, and a group. ﴿And the believers﴾: by this he meant the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers). ﴿Believe in what has been sent down to you﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. ﴿And what was sent down before you﴾, meaning: the rest of the revealed Books. ﴿And those who establish the prayer﴾. There is a difficulty here from the standpoint of grammar (nahw). It was said that this refers to Aisha and Aban ibn Uthman, and they both claimed that the scribe had made an error, and said: it should be written "wal-muqimun al-salah" (in the nominative). But it is not so; rather it is correct in grammar, and it is in the accusative of praise (nasb ala al-madh), and its implied sense is: "and mention those who establish the prayer," or "I mean those who establish the prayer." They are those who give the zakat. A similar example is the poet's saying:

(The alighters in every battlefield... and the good ones [the knots] of the waistwraps)

That is, I mean the alighters in every battlefield, and they are the good ones, the knots of the waistwraps; so it is in the accusative of praise. It was also said that its implied sense is: "and what was sent down to those who establish the prayer." His saying: ﴿And those who give the zakat﴾ returns to the original construction. ﴿And the believers in Allah and the Last Day, those — We will give them a great reward﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 163:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾. This is built upon what preceded in His saying ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven﴾. Allah, exalted is He, says: We have made you a messenger by the same means by which We made all the other prophets messengers, namely revelation (al-wahy), ﴿and We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Tribes and Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon﴾. He mentions a number of the messengers to whom He revealed.

If someone says: Why did He mention Jesus first, when he came later? It is said: the particle "wa" (and) does not necessarily imply order; it only denotes joining together. It is also said: he mentioned him out of concern for his affair, since the matter of Jesus was of greater importance. ﴿And We gave David a Psalter﴾. Hamzah recited "Zabūran" with a damma on the letter zay. So "zabūr" is on the pattern fa'ūl in the sense of maf'ūl (passive participle), and it is the book which Allah, exalted is He, sent down to David, containing glorification, exaltation, and praise of Allah, exalted is He. "Zabūr" also means writing, and "zibra" means a piece of iron. It is said: "mā lahu zabr," meaning he has no intellect. As for "zubūr," it is the plural of "zibr."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 164:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And messengers We have already related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you﴾ — We sent messengers, some of whom We have related to you before, ﴿and [some] messengers We have not related to you. And Allah spoke to Moses with [direct] speech﴾. He spoke to him Himself, without any intermediary and without any inspiration. This is evidence against the one who says that God created speech in the tree, and Moses heard it, because He said: ﴿And Allah spoke to Moses with [direct] speech﴾. Al-Farra' and Tha'lab said: The Arabs call whatever reaches a person "speech" by whatever route it reaches him, but they do not qualify it with the verbal noun (al-masdar). When speech is qualified with the verbal noun, it can only be the true reality of speech. This is like volition (al-irada): it is said "So-and-so willed a volition (irada)," which is the true reality of volition. But one does not say "The wall willed to fall, a volition (irada)"; rather one says "The wall willed (aradа)," without mentioning the verbal noun, because it is figurative. So when Allah qualified His speech to Moses with [the verbal noun] "speaking" (taklim), it became known that it is the true reality of speech without an intermediary. Tha'lab said: This is evidence for the view of al-Farra' that he did not hold that the Qur'an is created.

If someone says: By what did Moses know that it was the speech of Allah? It is said: By Allah, exalted is He, informing him of it, and by sending down a sign by which Moses knew that it was the speech of Allah, exalted is He. This is the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah: that he heard the speech of Allah in reality, without asking how. Wa'il ibn Dawud said: The meaning of His saying, ﴿And Allah spoke to Moses with [direct] speech﴾ is: repeatedly, speech after speech.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 165:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and as warners﴾, meaning: We sent messengers ﴿so that people would have no argument against God after the messengers﴾. This is evidence that God, may He be exalted, does not punish creation before He sends messengers, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We would not punish until We send a messenger﴾. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾.

﴿And God is ever Mighty﴾, meaning: capable of aiding creation, ﴿Wise﴾ in sending the messengers. In the hadith of Abu al-Darda', he said: "I asked the Messenger of God about the number of the prophets, and he said: 'One hundred and twenty-four thousand.' I said: 'How many of them were messengers?' He said: 'Three hundred and fifteen, a great throng.'"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 166:

Allah's words, ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse: a group of scholars of the Jews came before the Prophet, and he said to them: "Do you know that I am the Messenger of Allah?" They said: "We do not know that." Then there was revealed His words: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾. That is: "with His knowledge," as one says: "So-and-so came to me with his sword," meaning: "with his sword." In this there is evidence that Allah has knowledge, which is one of His attributes, contrary to the saying of the Mu'tazilah (a theological school that denied God's attributes), may Allah disgrace them.

﴿And the angels bear witness, and Allah is sufficient as a witness﴾. If it is asked: if Allah bears witness to his prophethood, what need is there for the testimony of the angels? It is said: because those who came before the Prophet thought of themselves as the scholars of the earth; they said: "We are the scholars of the earth, and we deny your messengership." So Allah the Exalted said: "If the scholars of the earth deny it, the scholars of the heavens, who are the angels, will bear witness to it, in opposition to their claim and their assumption; not because there is a need for their testimony, for He said: ﴿and Allah is sufficient as a witness﴾."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who have disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah﴾. Their averting [others] from the way of Allah was by concealing the description of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Have certainly strayed into a far-off straying﴾. That is: they have perished, and ḍalāl (straying) means destruction.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 168:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged﴾. If someone says: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿and wronged﴾, when He has already said ﴿disbelieved﴾, and their wronging is their disbelief? It is said: its meaning is that they disbelieved in Allah, and they wronged Muhammad (ﷺ) by concealing his description.

It is also said: He mentioned it as emphasis. ﴿Allah would not forgive them﴾ — in this there is an indication that Allah, exalted is He, if He had forgiven all the disbelievers, His mercy would have been wide enough for that, but He has decreed the word that He will not forgive them, ﴿nor guide them to a path﴾, meaning: to Islam.

Translation:

﴿Except the road of Hell,﴾ meaning: Judaism, ﴿wherein they will abide forever. And that is ever easy for Allah.﴾

Almighty God's saying: ﴿O mankind, the Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you.﴾ Its implied meaning: belief would be better for you. ﴿And if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 171:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O People of the Book, do not commit excess in your religion﴾. Ghuluww (excessiveness, going beyond the limit) means exceeding the bound. The verse is about the Christians. Al-Hasan said: it is permissible that it applies to both the Jews and the Christians, for they went to excess regarding the matter of ʿIsa (Jesus). As for the Jews, it was by falling short in his due; as for the Christians, it was by exceeding the limit concerning him.

Ghuluww is not praiseworthy in religion. Ibn ʿAbbas narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Beware of excessiveness in religion, for those before you were destroyed only through excessiveness."

﴿And do not say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, ʿIsa son of Maryam, is only the messenger of Allah and His word﴾. We have already explained the views of the scholars concerning his being a "word," and there are three opinions on the meaning of his being "His word." The first: that he came into being by His word, which is His saying "Be," and he was. The second: that he is guided by it, just as one is guided by the word of Allah. The third: "His word" means His glad tidings, which were given in the scriptures: "There shall be ʿIsa." This is the meaning of His saying: (﴿and His word, which He cast to Maryam and a spirit from Him﴾). And concerning his being called a "spirit," there are three opinions. The first: that he had a spirit like all other spirits, except that Allah, exalted is He, attributed it to Himself as an honour.

The second: that hearts are given life through him, just as bodies are given life through the spirit.

The third: that the spirit is the breath which Jibril (Gabriel) blew into Maryam by the permission of Allah; so that breath was called a spirit.

﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say "Three."﴾ The Christians used to say "Three"; they would say: Son, Father, and Holy Spirit. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They have certainly disbelieved who said, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three."﴾ And His saying: ﴿Cease, it is better for you.﴾ Its implied meaning: let ceasing be better for you.

﴿Allah is but one God; exalted is He above having a son.﴾ Know that just as it is not permissible for Allah to take a son, adoption is also not permissible for Him, for adoption occurs only where there can be a child. Since it is not conceivable that Allah has a child, and adoption is not permissible concerning Him, ﴿to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 172:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah﴾. Istinkaf (disdain) is arrogance accompanied by aversion (al-anfah), and its meaning is: the Messiah will never be averse to being a servant. ﴿Nor will the angels brought near.﴾ Those who hold that the angels are superior to humankind have cited this verse as evidence, because Allah, exalted be He, ascended from Jesus to the angels. But there is no evidence in the verse. Rather, He said "nor the angels brought near" not because of the impossibility of their station and rank being above the station of humans, but He said that according to what the Christians hold. It may be that they believed the angels were superior to humans, so He said that according to their assumption.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will gather them to Himself all together.﴾ The difference between istinkaf and istikbar is that istinkaf is arrogance accompanied by aversion, while istikbar is excessive pride (al-ghuluww), arrogance without aversion.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 4, verse 173:

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty.﴾ It was said: the increase of His bounty is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

It was also said: it is intercession. In a hadith: "The righteous will intercede on the Day of Resurrection for those whom they know."

﴿As for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any ally or any helper.﴾

Almighty God's saying: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord﴾. It was said: it is Muhammad (ﷺ); most of the commentators hold this view. And it was said: it is the Qur'an.

Al-burhan (proof, clear evidence) in the language is the argument (al-hujjah). ﴿And We have sent down to you a clear light﴾: it is the Qur'an.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿As for those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him, He will admit them to mercy from Him and bounty﴾ — meaning Paradise — ﴿and guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 176:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you for a legal decision. Say: Allah gives you a decision concerning the kalalah (one who leaves neither ascendants nor descendants)﴾. It is narrated from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib that he said: The last surah to be revealed in its entirety was Surat Bara'ah, and the last verse to be revealed was this verse.

﴿If there are two sisters, they shall have two-thirds of what he left. And if there are siblings, men and women, then the male shall have the equivalent of the share of two females.﴾

The occasion of revelation of the verse is what has been narrated: "The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon Jabir while he was ill and had lost consciousness. He asked for water, performed ablution, and then sprinkled it on him, and he regained consciousness. Jabir said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what should I do with my property, since only a kalalah inherits from me?' Then the verse was revealed." The discussion of the kalalah has already passed.

That verse (the first) concerns the inheritance of siblings from the mother, and this verse concerns the inheritance of siblings from both parents, and from the father. ﴿If a man dies leaving no child﴾ its meaning: he has no child, nor a father. On this view most scholars hold that the kalalah is this, and that brothers and sisters do not inherit alongside the father, except what is related from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he gave them inheritance alongside the father, and this has already passed.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿he has no child﴾ he intended by it: a male child. On this view most scholars hold that brothers and sisters do not inherit alongside a son, but they do inherit alongside a daughter. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, and Dawud and the Zahiris also held this, adhering to the apparent wording of the verse: that brothers and sisters do not inherit alongside a daughter. We have explained that what is meant by it is a son, and the verse concerns the negation of the fixed share alongside a child. In our view, they inherit only as residuaries (ta'sib), since sisters alongside daughters are residuaries.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if a man or a woman leaves neither heirs nor ascendants, and he has a brother or a sister, then each one of them shall have a sixth. But if they are more than that, they shall share in a third. After any bequest that is made or debt, without causing harm. This is a commandment from Allah, and Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.﴾ — This is a different verse; the text here reads: ﴿And he has a sister, then she shall have half of what he left, and he inherits from her if she has no child. If there are two sisters, then they shall have two-thirds of what he left. And if there are siblings, men and women, then the male shall have the equivalent of the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray.﴾

Al-Farra' said: its meaning is: Allah makes clear to you that you not go astray. This is also the view of Abu 'Ubayd. Abu 'Ubayd said: al-Kisa'i mentioned a hadith with this meaning and was pleased with it, namely what is narrated from the Prophet that he said: "Let none of you pray against his son that he coincide with a decree," meaning: that he not coincide with a decree.

The Basrans said: its meaning is: Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray (i.e., out of dislike that you go astray). ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything.﴾

And Allah knows best. Allah has spoken truly, and His Messenger has spoken truly, and upon his family, all of them.
